Cybersecurity and automation giant Infoblox has confirmed a cybersecurity incident, during which hackers accessed company information through one of its technology vendors.

Infoblox is a privately held cyber giant that provides companies cybersecurity and networking services, such as domain name resolution, and identity and user access management.

In a statement, a spokesperson for Infoblox told TechCrunch that the company is “investigating a security event involving unauthorized access to certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor.”

“We immediately activated our incident response procedures, took steps to contain the incident and are working with leading outside cybersecurity experts to investigate the facts, understand the scope and address any confirmed risks.”

TechCrunch has learned that the data breach involves a vendor that provides SharePoint data migration services, according to a notification sent by Infoblox about the breach, two people with knowledge of the incident told TechCrunch.

One of the people said sensitive customer data was taken in the breach.

According to public internet records seen by TechCrunch, Infoblox hosts much of its files, emails and infrastructure with Microsoft, including a SharePoint server, which TechCrunch confirmed is accessible through Infoblox’s single sign-on provider. SharePoint is web-based software that companies use to share and host internal files and documents.

Infoblox has not named the third-party migration vendor that was hacked, but one person with knowledge of the incident said that Infoblox has terminated its work with the vendor.

The company’s spokesperson did not comment on this, but added that the company has “no indication that any Infoblox products, cloud services, software updates or build-and-release processes were involved” in the breach.

Infoblox would not say how many customers were affected by the incident, or if the company is aware at this time. The company also did not say, when asked, if it had been contacted by the hackers and if they had made any demands.

Nvidia interim CEO and long-time CFO Colette Kress is about to have one of the biggest days of her career on Tuesday when the company reports its third-quarter results.

For the first time, Kress will be running through the numbers and sharing guidance without Nvidia’s charismatic but now-disgraced founder Jensen Huang.

Huang was forced to resign last week after he admitted to having an affair with an exec of a customer, Alice Huang, a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, and he was accused of having two more affairs with Nvidia employees.

Now, the company is facing questions about its restricted chips allegedly being smuggled into China, especially by Huang’s mistress’s company. Nvidia promised to conduct an internal investigation. Meanwhile, Huang was commanded to answer questions to Congress in a closed-door joint session with three Republican-led committees. Plus, top Democrats have also vowed to investigate the company.

Given the turmoil Nvidia is in, there are a number of questions that Kress should answer.

Huang’s role now and going forward. Huang ran Nvidia with an iron fist, having some 60 direct reports and his fingers in everything. No one knows the company better than him.

An internet petition signed by 180,000 and growing is calling for the board to reinstate him. Huang may also have been mounting an attempt to return, the Financial Times reported. However, CNBC is reporting, citing unnamed sources, that the company is not in talks to reinstate Huang.

So, we’ll be looking for language from the interim CEO about Huang’s ongoing involvement with the company, its search for a new CEO and any talks to bring him back.

China and Singapore. As Huang vehemently argued in favor of easing export restrictions for Nvidia chips to China, Huang said that he’s seen no evidence that its powerful semiconductors were being diverted from legit buyers to China.

But in October 2025, The New York Times reported that the U.S. was investigating Huang’s mistress’s company, Megaspeed, over allegations it was doing just that. Nvidia at the time vouched to CNBC that Megaspeed was legally using the chips for its cloud. However, Nvidia recently told The Wall Street Journal that it had voluntarily blocked Megaspeed from receiving more chips way back in June 2025.

Last year, Nvidia said that Singapore, the region where Megaspeed was located, was one of its fastest-growing, accounting for 22% of its total revenue for its second quarter of that year. After the investigation into Megaspeed came to light, Nvidia changed how it reported revenue. It now reports based on a company’s headquarters, instead of its shipping address. That completely hid sales to Singapore and Megaspeed’s impact.

So we’re listening to what Kress says about the future of sales to the China region and the cloud business in Singapore that was once 20% of sales. We’re especially listening for what she says about Nvidia keeping track of where its restricted chips wind up.

China sales policy . Huang’s argument was, essentially, that the U.S. can’t stop China from developing advanced AI models, so the West is better off selling them less powerful Nvidia chips and keeping them dependent, he said on the Dwarkesh Podcast last summer. Notably, that’s a position that would make Nvidia a lot of money.

The China hawks counter that selling an adversary any powerful chips at all will help them, and U.S. companies shouldn’t do that. So we’re listening for any indications that Kress is reversing Nvidia’s goals with China.

Bankrolling the AI build-out. The expectation is that Kress, the CFO who reportedly had unsuccessfully tried to push back against Huang’s extreme AI dealmaking, will be conservative on such deals going forward. We’ll be listening for what she says about the impacts of existing deals on the books. (Will she subtly try to throw Huang under the bus for those controversial deals ?) We’ll also be listening for her future plans.

Governance. With the ousting of Huang and more fallout sure still to come , has the board learned its lesson about too much power in the hands of one person? We’ll be listening for information about how Nvidia might restructure itself.

As promised last month , Apple on Monday announced changes to Mac security controls designed to protect users’ data from the growing popularity of AI agents and their apps’ demand for “full disk access.”

“Before granting an app such extraordinary access, users should understand that it puts all of the data on their Mac at risk,” Apple wanred in a new blog post aimed at app developers.

Unlike AI chatbots that simply answer questions, agents run on a user’s device where they can take actions across the operating system, files, and apps on the user’s behalf.

While the tools can be useful, Apple has grown concerned about the increased risks to users’ data and privacy that these AI agents introduce. At the same time, the company has been benefiting from sales of Mac minis and Mac Studio computers that AI early adopters have been purchasing specifically to run their local AI models.

To balance these competing interests, Apple said in October that it would revise some of its security settings around Mac apps. The announcement followed two notable incidents involving AI agents. In one, a journalist claimed that Meta’s Muse app read their private messages without consent; a separate report from Wired cited a flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac app that could have allowed hackers to access sensitive data.

Now, Apple is sharing the changes it’s making.

For starters, it’s splitting up Device Control and Data Access into two settings: System & App Protection Override and Accessibility. The changes is designed to help users better understand that selecting the first option means overriding built-in security protections.

To streamline configurations, Apple says there will now also be a single method for granting permissions that involves selecting the requested app from a list. The company will also introduce new guidance encouraging users to grant access only to the specific apps that need it when they enable the System & App Protection Override setting. Similar guidance will appear when users enable Full Disk Access to allow an app to access their folders.

The company will also provide users with “increased visibility into the wide range of data apps will receive access to or control over if full permissions are granted,” the blog post notes.

Another change will give users more granular control over when an AI agent or app can gain access by allowing users to configure their apps to ask for permission every time access is needed. While arguably tedious and a potential obstacle to true automation, the feature could allow users to experiment with local AI without giving the agent carte blanche.

There will also be a new transparency indicator that appears when an app is controlling another app through the System & App Protection Override option.

The changes, which are arriving with macOS 27.3, don’t appear to prevent Mac users from installing and running AI agents or other apps that ask for higher levels of access. Instead, they give users more nuanced options, control, and information about the choices they’re making.

Apple advises app developers to adjust their onboarding processes to account for the new changes and suggests that their apps learn to “gracefully handle having access to only a limited set of folders or apps.”

Developers of apps that request Full Disk Access for disk backup or to provide assistive technologies can request exceptions to the new rules (which Apple calls “entitlements”) to preserve the same functionality they offered before the macOS 27.3 update.

items.title: Trump’s accounts traded up to $97.5 million in Nvidia as Huang gained White House access
items.summary: Trump’s accounts sold up to $1 million in Nvidia stock five days after he was briefed on Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.

scraped.title: Trump’s accounts traded up to $97.5 million in Nvidia as Huang gained White House access
scraped.description: Trump’s accounts sold up to $1 million in Nvidia stock five days after he was briefed on Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
scraped.author: Luke Fountain
scraped.h1: Trump’s accounts traded up to $97.5 million in Nvidia as Huang gained White House access
scraped.body_text:
In this article

President Donald Trump has had plenty of reason to cheer the rise of Nvidia .

The chipmaker helped propel the stock market that Trump is fond of touting. Its billionaire co-founder, Jensen Huang , became one of the president's favorite businessmen. And by the end of last year, Nvidia had become one of Trump's three largest individual stock holdings, worth between $12.5 million and $58 million, up from between $615,000 and $1.3 million a year earlier.

Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have bought or sold Nvidia shares at least 103 times — transactions worth a combined $27 million to $97.5 million, according to a new CNBC analysis of his annual and periodic financial disclosures, which were most recently updated through August.

By midday Monday, Trump's Nvidia stake, based on the value he reported holding in August, would be worth $4.5 million to $57.7 million with stock priced around $157. But the filings give broad dollar ranges for holdings rather than the number of shares, leaving his current stake unclear.

Now, Huang's resignation as Nvidia's CEO on Thursday, following revelations about his relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China and reports of affairs with company employees, has put those trades back in the spotlight.

Among them was a sale of $500,001 to $1 million on May 18 , the first Monday after Trump returned from a state visit to China with Huang. Five days earlier, before Huang boarded Air Force One during a refueling stop in Alaska, Secretary of State Marco Rubio had briefed Trump on intelligence concerning Huang's relationship with the suspected spy, The New York Times reported .

Trump on Monday denied being briefed . Asked about the reported briefing from Rubio, Trump said, "I haven't heard that," adding that he did not know whether the woman, Alice Huang, was a Chinese spy.

The president's financial accounts also bought smaller amounts of Nvidia shares in the days immediately before and after the May 18 sale, part of a broader trading blitz . Such flurries have defined his second term: Trump disclosed more than 21,000 trades in 2025 alone , compared with roughly 500 during his entire first term, according to CNBC's analysis.

A White House spokesperson told CNBC independent advisors manage Trump's portfolio without his input. Trump Organization spokesperson Kimberly Benza said the arrangement is designed to "avoid even the appearance of a conflict of interest." The disclosures offer no evidence Trump directed the trades or that his advisors had access to classified intelligence.

Trump has long used the stock market as a scorecard for the economy, touting its record highs — sometimes when highs have not actually been reached — despite the turbulence caused by his tariffs and the Iran war .

"Look, we have the highest stock market we've ever had," Trump told ESPN commentator and political talk show host Stephen A. Smith on Thursday when pressed about Republicans' midterm losses .

Nvidia alone accounted for about 13.5% of the S&P 500's 2026 gains through September, according to an analysis by Choate Wealth that looked at how chip stocks have driven the year's performance.

Huang's rise in Trump's Washington has been nearly as striking as Nvidia's on Wall Street. The two have met or appeared together at least 15 times since Trump returned to office, according to a CNBC review of public records and news reports. Huang in June told The Associated Press that Trump even "calls me in the middle of the night."

It wasn't always that way.

At Trump's Jan. 20, 2025, inauguration, several Silicon Valley titans occupied prime seats, but Huang wasn't there. The two men had never met.

That changed on Jan. 31, 2025, when Huang visited the White House, capping a bruising week for Nvidia: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek had wiped $593 billion off the company's market value in a single day, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters .

Two days before the meeting, Trump's money managers bought between $1 million and $5 million in Nvidia stock .

For Huang, much of the relationship hinged on access to China. In April 2025, the administration effectively halted sales of Nvidia's H20 chips to China, prompting a $4.5 billion charge , according to an SEC filing. Huang argued that withholding U.S. chips would only accelerate China's development of its own.

The administration eventually relented. After another meeting with Trump in July 2025, Huang announced from Beijing that Nvidia expected to resume H20 sales . A week after Trump confirmed an August 2025 deal calling for 15% of the revenue from the company's chip sales to China to go to the U.S. government, his accounts also bought between $5 million and $25 million in Nvidia stock, one of several large tech investments that day.

Huang was also becoming a fixture of Trump's international diplomacy, joining him in Saudi Arabia and the U.K. Nvidia, already a $1 million donor to Trump's inaugural fund , would pledge another $25 million to his planned White House ballroom on condition of anonymity, The Washington Post first reported .

But behind the scenes, intelligence officials first briefed Trump last fall on Huang's relationship with the woman suspected of spying for China, The New York Times reported .

Trump nevertheless continued to ease restrictions on Nvidia's business in China, announcing Dec. 8 that the company could sell its more powerful H200 chips . His accounts had sold as much as $1 million in Nvidia stock four days earlier and bought more the day after.

In the first eight months of 2026, Trump's accounts made another 38 Nvidia trades worth a combined $9.4 million to $28.3 million, according to CNBC's analysis. A disclosure released Oct. 8 — the day Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science — showed purchases of up to $1.6 million and sales of up to $1 million in August alone.

Trump stood by Huang as Nvidia's board weighed his future last week, urging him to fight to keep his job , the Times reported.

With Huang out and Nvidia's shares tumbling, Trump described him Thursday as a "tremendous talent" who was "going through hell" — in the same interview in which he boasted of the market's record highs.

Trump is already floating a comeback for Huang, telling reporters Monday that reinstating him "certainly isn't a bad idea." But Nvidia's board is not considering his return , a person familiar with the matter told CNBC. The person asked not to be named because they were discussing internal matters."

scraped.author: Sara Salinas
scraped.h1: JPMorgan Chase says temporary software bug is affecting consumer banking
scraped.body_text:
In this article

JPMorgan Chase reported a "technical issue" that was affecting some consumer banking services Monday.

The bank said a "temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems" was causing some customer transactions to take longer than usual, though it said customers can still access their accounts and funds.

"There is no evidence it is cyber-related," a JPMorgan spokesperson said in a statement to CNBC.

"This is not a systemic issue — other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," the spokesperson said. "We're working diligently to resolve this by the end of the day today."

CNBC's Eamon Javers reported there was no indication of bad actors involved.

Still, other major banks were listed in outage reports as transactions between Chase and other institutions appeared to get held up. Users reported errors as early as 11:30 a.m. ET.

A representative for U.S. Bank said that company was "not directly impacted. However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays."

Zelle is the peer-to-peer payments system backed by many of the largest U.S. banks, including JPMorgan.

The outage reports come days after separate, widespread issues with Microsoft Outlook and communication systems used by air traffic control centers .

— CNBC's Leslie Picker contributed to this report.

scraped.author: Fred Imbert
scraped.h1: Berkshire Hathaway raised its stake in Delta in the third quarter. It also trimmed a key bank holding
scraped.body_text:
In this article

Berkshire Hathaway made several moves in the stock market during the third quarter, adding to key positions and trimming others.

The Greg Abel-led conglomerate increased its Delta Air Lines stake by 12%, scooping up 7.13 million shares. The position was worth $5.37 billion at the end of the third quarter.

Delta shares tumbled 11% over that period, as rising jet fuel prices due to the U.S.-Iran war pressured the airline industry. That marked the stock's worst quarterly performance since the first quarter of 2025, when it plunged 28%. Delta last month also cut its full-year earnings forecast , citing a surge in fuel costs.

To be sure, buying that dip has been a winning investment thus far. Delta is up 3.8% so far in the fourth quarter, while the S&P 500 has dropped 3.1%. Shares are also up nearly 15% over the past month.

Berkshire also trimmed its holding in Bank of America by nearly 6%, selling more than $1.6 billion worth of stock.

BofA was under pressure in the third quarter, falling more than 4%, as interest rates surged alongside stubbornly high inflation and expectations of tighter Federal Reserve monetary policy. At one point in September the 30-year Treasury bond yield surged above 5.6% to its highest level since 2002 .

Despite the share sale, Bank of America remains a top Berkshire Hathaway holding, with the conglomerate's stake valued at $24.8 billion at the end of the third quarter.

Berkshire also initiated a position in Bending Spoons and nearly doubled its stake in homebuilder Lennar in the latest quarter.

items.summary: It’s not a question of 'if' but 'how' Canada wants to deepen economic cooperation with China, experts say, as Carney continues push for trade diversification.

scraped.title: How Carney’s China visit highlights the stakes—and risks—of closer ties - National | Globalnews.ca
scraped.description: It’s not a question of 'if' but 'how' Canada wants to deepen economic cooperation with China, experts say, as Carney continues push for trade diversification.
scraped.h1: How Carney’s China visit highlights the stakes—and risks—of closer ties
scraped.body_text:
Instructions:

Name

Δ

6 comments

@Ben. There is no balancing act. The goods sold to China are much different than those that go to the USA.

Always need to remember that China is a communist country. People are jailed for speaking up against them and they are anti Christian.

Long term negative consequences for Canada should they get closer to China. This is a foolish choice.

Carney is balancing China against the US.

As an Albertan I prefer working with the USA over China.

More theatre for his useful idiots

It’s not a question of “if” but “how” Prime Minister Mark Carney will seek to deepen economic ties with China amidst a global reordering provoked by U.S. President Donald Trump, experts say.

Carney is set to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday, the two leaders’ second meetings since Carney was elected in part on a promise to diversify Canadian trade away from the U.S.

China is a significant part of that strategy. After years of diplomatic hostilities — including China’s arrest and detention of Michael Kovrig and Michael Spavor — the Carney government signed a “strategic partnership” with Beijing to collaborate on energy and clean technology.

Deanna Horton, Canada’s former ambassador to Vietnam and a fellow at the Munk School of Global Affairs, said there’s a “great deal at stake” in the Canada-China relationship given the trade tensions with Trump’s administration.

Horton said despite the Democrats dramatic victory in this month’s midterm elections, she thinks it’s unlikely that Canada and the U.S. will return to the kind of tariff-free trade the two countries enjoyed in the past.

“We’re evolving into G2 world, the U.S. and China, and Canada needs to not have all its eggs in the U.S. basket,” Horton, who was also involved in the negotiations of the original North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), said in an interview Monday.

“I don’t think we’re in a position now where we’re going to not want to deepen relations in China. I don’t think that is really an option for Canada. The question is: where do we place the emphasis in terms of improving relationships?”

Much of the attention around the meeting has been focused on Canada’s auto sector, already hurting from Trump’s trade war and bracing for higher tariffs in the new year.

In a January 2026 deal, Canada reduced its 100 per cent tariff on Chinese electric vehicles to 6.1 per cent and allowed up to 49,000 of the vehicles to be sold annually, with the cap increasing over time.

China agreed to lower tariffs on Canadian agricultural goods as a result.

Speaking to reporters in Cambodia Monday, Carney said that depending on what happens with U.S. trade talks, Canada could look elsewhere — including to China — to bolster its automotive industry.

“(Canada has) great autoworkers; important market, real assets in Canada. If they’re not fully utilized in a North American context, that provides other opportunities,” Carney said.

“Canada is going to move forward either way.”

Margaret McCuaig-Johnston, a senior fellow at the University of Ottawa and a leading expert on Canada-China relations, said Carney’s talk of greater Chinese involvement in the Canadian auto industry may be a bargaining move as talks with the U.S. stretch on.

“That, in my view, would be encouraging. If it’s a bargaining chip, it can be dropped,” McCuaig-Johnston said in an interview Monday.

“If it’s an offer to China to open up our manufacturing to them, that’s got a lot of concerns. They don’t want to use Canadian parts, they don’t want to follow Canadian labour standards … and they don’t want technology transfer (to Canadian companies).”

McCuaig-Johnston said those factors were the “guardrails” the federal government often talks about when it comes to protecting Canada’s auto sector while allowing greater Chinese investment.

And while Carney and the government talk about “guardrails” in other sectors — such as critical minerals and defence — McCuaig-Johnston said what those protections are is not exactly clear.

Beyond the economic relationship, Carney also said he would raise the issue of Chinese foreign interference in Canadian political affairs with Xi.

The Canadian intelligence community has repeatedly warned that China, among other countries, has attempted to covertly interfere in Canadian politics, as well as engage in transnational repression against Chinese diaspora groups living Canada.

Carney himself said just last year that China was one of the greatest threat to Canadian national security.

“The advantage of these meetings is you can raise these issues directly and frankly. And I will be raising the importance with which we attach to the non-interference in our affairs by China and other countries,” Carney told reporters earlier this month.

Another meeting at this week’s APEC summit could be of keen interest to Canada and its foreign policy — the planned trilateral meeting between Xi, Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The meeting, which was proposed by Trump and accepted by Xi, is reportedly to discuss nuclear disarmament. The U.S. and Russia have the world’s largest stockpiles of nuclear weapons, and China has balked at talks of nuclear de-escalation.

China’s foreign ministry said on Monday that the meeting will be of “groundbreaking significance” and will promote peace and stability.

With files from the Associated Press and Reuters.

Britain’s Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales , have arrived in India for a short three-day visit; the first overseas trip the couple has made together since the princess’s cancer diagnosis in 2024.

The Prince and Princess of Wales’ visit began in Mumbai, where they will attend the Earthshot Prize awards ceremony on Tuesday. The environmental prize, founded by Prince William, awards five winners $1.3 million each to develop climate change solutions.

Tuesday’s ceremony is expected to be the largest since the prize was established in 2020 and will feature various notable attendees, including actor Rami Malek and iconic British pop group Take That, which is making its debut performance in India.

Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar is also set to attend.

“India has made an extraordinary contribution to Earthshot over the past six years and is home to more Earthshot finalists and winners than any other country,” the future king posted on social media.

“Too often the world’s emerging economies are presented with false choices: growth or the environment, prosperity or protection, but India shows us a different picture. A picture full of colour, complexity and possibility,” he said during a speech at the Earthshot Prize Impact Assembly on Monday.

One of the finalists has developed a solution to help stop the spread of natural disasters by using AI and thermal satellite imaging to detect fires early and alert emergency services. The technology operates across 92 million hectares in 21 countries and identifies fires 35 minutes faster than NASA on average.

Shortly after their arrival, the royal couple participated in a game of street cricket in a Mumbai neighbourhood. Street cricket is an integral part of everyday life in Mumbai. They also took a trip on Mumbai’s newest metro line and met with female workers supporting its infrastructure and public transport developments in India.

The couple are also set to attend events celebrating the country’s cricket, fashion and film industries before travelling to New Delhi, where they are scheduled to meet with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The couple last met with Modi when Queen Elizabeth II was still alive.

Their trip marks a return to international travel for the Princess of Wales, who announced her cancer diagnosis in March 2024. In January 2025, she said she was in remission and began making a gradual return to public duties.

In May, she travelled to Italy without her husband; it was her first international engagement since her diagnosis.

Earlier this year, the Princess of Wales completed the Three Peaks Challenge in aid of the cancer centre where she was treated, making her the first member of the Royal Family to climb the U.K.’s highest mountains in 24 hours.

She was treated at the Royal Marsden Hospital in Chelsea, west London, a specialist oncology hospital.

The Three Peaks challenge is a popular endurance challenge that involves climbing Ben Nevis, Scafell Pike and Mount Snowdon — in Scotland, England and Wales, respectively — within 24 hours.

She climbed all three climbs alone, but was supported on the way by mountain rescue teams and greeted at the top by her husband and their three children, Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis; her parents, Carole and Michael Middleton; and her brother, James Middleton.

— with files from the Associated Press

scraped.body_text:

Russia just needs more motivation to leave Ukraine…more boom bahs !

Zelensky doesn’t want the war to end The longer it continues the more money he makes

Ukrainian drones struck a bridge over the Kerch Strait linking Russia and Crimea overnight on Monday, but damage was minor, and repairs would be quick, Russian officials said.

Officials in Crimea, a peninsula jutting into the Black Sea annexed by Russia from Ukraine in 2014, said a single lane of traffic on the bridge had resumed by mid-evening, roughly 17 hours after it was closed.

Road traffic was allowed through by alternating directions while trains were operating normally, they said.

“We have already gathered together the resources, designers, and builders for repair work. We are sorting out logistics issues with the regional leadership,” Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin wrote on Telegram.

“We will organize all the work the way it needs to be done. As I said, we have the experience.”

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov had earlier described damage to the bridge as minor.

The 19-km (12-mile) Crimea Bridge is the only direct link between the transport networks of Russia and Crimea.

It has in the past been a key supply route for Russian forces in Ukraine and is widely viewed as one of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s signature infrastructure projects.

It consists of a separate roadway and railway, both supported by concrete stilts, which give way to a wider span held by steel arches at the point where ships pass between the Black Sea and the smaller Azov Sea.

The bridge has been attacked by Ukraine several times since Putin sent Russian forces into Ukraine in February 2022. A truck bomb in October 2022 killed four people and limited the bridge’s capacity for several months.

The overnight strike followed an intensification of Russian attacks in the past few months on bridges in Ukraine, including in the capital Kyiv.

Few countries have recognized Crimea as part of the Russian Federation but the Kremlin has said the question has been closed “forever.”

scraped.title: HK students can apply to 169 mainland universities with DSE results from 2027
scraped.description: Four more mainland higher education institutions have been added to a scheme allowing Hong Kong students to seek admission based on their DSE results from 2027, bringing the total number of participating schools to 169.
scraped.author: Hans Tse
scraped.h1: Four more mainland Chinese universities to admit Hong Kong students on DSE results from 2027
scraped.body_text:
Hong Kong Free Press HKFP

Hong Kong news, breaking updates – 100% Independent, impartial, non-profit

Four more mainland higher education institutions have been added to a scheme allowing Hong Kong students to seek admission based on their DSE results from 2027, bringing the total number of participating schools to 169.

China’s Ministry of Education announced on Monday that the number of institutions participating in the Scheme for Admission of Hong Kong Students to Mainland Higher Education Institutions will increase to 169 for the 2027/28 academic year.

The institutions are located in 21 provinces or municipalities and the autonomous regions of Inner Mongolia and Guangxi Zhuang.

The four newly participating institutions are Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics, Lishui University, Guangzhou Xinhua University and Fuyao University of Science and Technology.

The scheme accepts the Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education (DSE) exam results and exempts Hong Kong students from taking China’s joint entrance examination – a special university entrance exam designed for students from Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan as opposed to the notoriously competitive national exam, known as the Gaokao.

A spokesperson for the Education Bureau (EDB) said these mainland institutions offered diverse programmes and encouraged Hong Kong students to consider them for higher education.

“We encourage Hong Kong students to pursue further studies on the Chinese Mainland through the Admission Scheme and seize the opportunity to learn about the country’s latest social, economic and cultural landscape, and plan ahead for their future development,” the spokesperson said in a statement.

The scheme also features a principal nomination mechanism allowing secondary school principals to nominate up to eight students. Under this track, applicants must achieve at least an “attained” grade in Citizenship and Social Development and a minimum total score of eight across the three core subjects – Chinese Language, English Language and Mathematics – with no score below two in any of those subjects.

Students can apply online from December 1 to 31 and confirm their application before January 10 next year. They should pay an application fee of HK$460 by January 31.

The Mainland Higher Education Expo 2027/28, jointly organised by the Office of Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan Affairs and the Department of College Students Affairs of the Ministry of Education, and the EDB, will be held on December 5 and 6.

Hong Kong has been encouraging local students to study in mainland China while increasing the intake of non-local students at its universities, many of whom come from the mainland.

Starting from the 2026/27 academic year, the enrolment limit for non-local students in self-financing programmes at the city’s publicly funded universities has been raised to 50 per cent of local student places.

scraped.description: A Yuen Long district councillor jailed for two and a half years for having unlawful intercourse with a girl under 16 has appealed against his conviction and sentence.
scraped.author: Hillary Leung
scraped.h1: Yuen Long district councillor appeals against conviction and 2.5-year jail term over unlawful sex with girl under 16
scraped.body_text:
Hong Kong Free Press HKFP

Hong Kong news, breaking updates – 100% Independent, impartial, non-profit

A Yuen Long district councillor jailed for two and a half years for having unlawful intercourse with a girl under 16 has appealed against his conviction and sentence.

Sei Chun-hing submitted his appeal application to the High Court on Friday, local media reported .

The 39-year-old was found guilty last month of having unlawful intercourse with a girl under 16, known to the court as X, over a decade ago.

He was acquitted of indecent assault against the same person, a verdict that the Department of Justice is appealing against, according to local media.

When Judge Stanley Chan handed down Sei’s sentence earlier this month, he said Sei had shown no regret over his actions and noted that the defence had not acknowledged the trauma experienced by X, who was in a relationship with Sei at the time.

Sei also did not use a condom during the 2013 incident, thereby exposing X to the risks of pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases, Chan said.

The maximum sentence for having unlawful intercourse with a girl under 16 but over the age of 13 is five years. For unlawful intercourse with a girl under 13, offenders face up to life imprisonment.

For indecent assault, the maximum sentence is 10 years. Jail terms for cases heard at the District Court, however, are capped at seven years.

Under Hong Kong law, a district councillor who is sentenced to a jail term longer than three months is disqualified. Sei, however, is still listed on the Yuen Long District Council website.

The government said in a statement after his jail term was handed down that Sei’s remuneration as a district councillor had been suspended since his conviction, and that a committee appointed by the government was conducting an investigation.

She worked at TIME Magazine in 2019, where she wrote about Asia and overnight US news before turning her focus to the protests that began that summer. At Coconuts Hong Kong, she covered general news and wrote features, including about a Black Lives Matter march that drew controversy amid the local pro-democracy movement and two sisters who were born to a domestic worker and lived undocumented for 30 years in Hong Kong.

scraped.title: Taiwan lawmaker critical of China in close race for Taipei mayor
scraped.description: A Taiwanese lawmaker wanted by police in China is running for Taipei mayor in an unexpectedly close race in the heartland of the Kuomintang party, which favours closer ties with Beijing.
scraped.author: AFP
scraped.h1: Taiwan lawmaker wanted by police in China closes gap in race for Taipei mayor
scraped.body_text:
Hong Kong Free Press HKFP

Hong Kong news, breaking updates – 100% Independent, impartial, non-profit

A Taiwanese lawmaker wanted by police in China is running for Taipei mayor in an unexpectedly close race in the heartland of the Kuomintang party, which favours closer ties with Beijing.

Campaigning in night markets, temples and motorcades is underway for the November 28 elections that will decide races for mayors, magistrates and other posts across the island democracy.

The Kuomintang party (KMT) won 14 of Taiwan’s 22 cities and counties — including Taipei — in a huge victory in 2022, while President Lai Ching-te’s Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) secured five seats.

Puma Shen, the 44-year-old DPP candidate in Taipei, is seeking to flip what has long been considered a safe KMT post and become the first DPP mayor of the capital in nearly 30 years.

Shen, who became a lawmaker in 2024, had been given little chance of beating KMT incumbent Chiang Wan-an, 47, who is seen as a rising star and future presidential candidate for Taiwan’s oldest party.

But recent voter surveys show Shen closing in on, or even slightly ahead, of Chiang.

See also: Taiwan accuses Hong Kong residents of hiring 4 people to spy on lawmaker critical of China

“I always believe I can win,” Shen told AFP in an interview at his office near Taiwan’s parliament, where he has been outspoken about Chinese influence and disinformation.

Shen is under investigation by police in China for alleged criminal “separatist activities” and is barred from entering the country.

Shen said his growing popularity among voters — which his campaign has dubbed an “Ocean Current”, in a play on the last character of his name — is partly due to his willingness to answer their questions.

“I think that’s the essence of democracy,” said Shen, who has used soapboxes and social media to engage directly with locals.

Chiang’s team declined AFP’s request for an interview with the mayor.

Albert Tzeng, a former KMT adviser, said the two candidates have very different personalities and political styles.

Chiang is a “decent politician” but “very conservative in articulating his view”, while Shen is more “outspoken” and better suited to social media, he said.

Voter surveys also show a potential major upset in the mayoral race in New Taipei City, Taiwan’s largest city and another KMT stronghold.

Losing Taipei and New Taipei City would be a blow for the KMT ahead of the 2028 presidential election when the party will seek to prevent the DPP from securing a fourth term.

Some in Lai’s government worry that KMT losses in the two key cities could embarrass Chinese leaders who have close ties with the party and will be watching the election.

Chinese President Xi Jinping met with Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun in April, the first KMT leader to visit China in a decade, in what was seen as his endorsement of her as head of the party.

A DPP victory in Taipei and New Taipei City might “look very concerning” to Beijing because it would show the party can gain seats previously seen as easy wins for the KMT, said Lev Nachman, a political science professor at National Taiwan University.

A poor performance by the KMT would also likely increase pressure on Cheng, whose strident pro-Beijing stance has angered many in her own party, to step down.

Most KMT candidates have kept their distance from Cheng during their campaigns and after the elections there will be a “very ugly struggle”, Tzeng predicted.

“There are many people who believe if Cheng Li-wun stays in power, the KMT will have zero chance in 2028.”

Analysts cautioned that local elections should not be seen as a predictor of how people might vote in the presidential race, with history showing repeatedly that it can be the reverse.

“The things they (voters) weigh in local elections differ from what they weigh in national-level elections,” Hsiao Yi-ching, director of the Election Study Center at National Chengchi University, told AFP.

“Local elections should be relatively less affected by cross-strait tensions and geopolitical or international political factors.”

Shen and Chiang have avoided talking about China during their campaigns, focusing instead on local issues such as urban renewal, transportation, childcare and artificial intelligence.

Lo Hui-fen, a 67-year-old retiree and supporter of Chiang, said he thought the mayor was “excellent” and had achieved a lot during his first term.

“To me, he is like the son next door,” Lo said at a night market where Chiang was holding a campaign event.

“He’s very approachable and willing to get things done.”

Shen supporter Jamie Cheng, 35, said the DPP candidate made her feel like he was listening.

“I can have a formal exchange with him,” Cheng, a digital designer, told AFP at a rally for the opening of Shen’s campaign office.

“It feels like my voice is being heard.”

Customers reported difficulty accessing the online accounts at some of the U.S.’ largest banks on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Bank of America, Chase, J.P. Morgan, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com.

Chase Bank’s services are experiencing a technical bug issue, not a cyber issue, a spokesperson said Monday (November 16, 2026).

“Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds,” a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. “We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible.”

The reports follow a major outage by Microsoft that began on Friday (November 13, 2026) and lasted for hours, which impacted services including Outlook, Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.

Some Chase customers received a message that said, “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”

Updated - November 17, 2026 03:36 am IST - Srinagar

Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha members burn an effigy during a protest over J&K Congress President Tariq Hameed Karra’s remarks on the mortal remains of two missing SPOs recovered at Kishtwar, in Jammu, on November 16, 2026. | Photo Credit: ANI

Two separate remarks made by J&K Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra and BJP legislator Shagun Parihar in the aftermath of the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar on Monday (November 16, 2026) sparked protests from different quarters.

In response to the statement by Mr. Karra that “two SPOs were killed reportedly by the Army in a mistaken identity case on November 11”, senior BJP leader and Leader of Opposition (LoP) Sunil Sharma said, “The Congress is spreading misleading information to shift the blame from terrorists to our security forces. The SPOs were on duty and travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah to relieve the jawans posted there. Calling two martyrs hunters is an insult to their sacrifice and to their grieving families.”

He demanded that Mr. Karra “immediately withdraw the remarks and apologise to the martyrs’ families, the J&K Police and the Indian Army”.

Scores of members of the BJP and BJP-affiliated organisations held street protests against Mr. Karra and the Congress in Jammu. Members of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) also burn an effigy of Mr. Karra as a mark of protest.

BJYM leader Arun Prabhat, while condemning the statement of Mr. Karra, said, “It shows the hearts of Congress beat for Pakistan. The conspirators should face action. In case of any role of mosques, such places too should face action.”

Mr. Prabhat was seconding the controversial remarks of Ms. Parihar of the BJP, who claimed “announcements were made from the mosques in Kishtwar’s Dachhan area to identify the targets” allegedly ahead of the killings of two SPOs on November 11.

However, several religious organisations, including the Anjuman Islamia Bhaderwah and Kishtwar, in the Chenab Valley condemned the statement of Ms. Parihar and denied any role of mosques in the latest attack on the policemen. Ruling National Conference (NC) legislator Tanvir Sadiq said the BJP must be “held accountable for its MLA’s deeply irresponsible and inflammatory allegations against a mosque in Jammu”.

“Making communal allegations in the aftermath of a tragic killing is utterly unacceptable. The BJP leadership cannot hide behind silence or pretend this is an isolated matter. It must unequivocally condemn these remarks and issue an unconditional public apology. Stop playing with the communal harmony of J&K,” said Mr. Sadiq.

A spokesman of the All J&K Shia Association said the organisation “strongly condemn Ms. Parihar’s attempt to drag a mosque into the tragic killing of our brave SPOs”. “Terrorists are enemies of all humanity and terrorism has no religion. Unsubstantiated claims against a place of worship only weaken our fight against terror,” said the Association.

Published - November 17, 2026 03:34 am IST

items.title: Woman Dies After Street Stabbing in Tokyo's Nakano
items.summary: A woman in her 20s was stabbed to death on a residential street near JR Nakano Station in Tokyo on the evening of November 16th, with police arresting a man in his 30s or 40s approximately 90 minutes later on suspicion of attempted robbery-murder after he allegedly attacked the woman with a knife and fled with her handbag. (News On Japan)

scraped.title: Woman Dies After Street Stabbing in Tokyo
scraped.description: A woman in her 20s was stabbed to death on a residential street near JR Nakano Station in Tokyo on the evening of November 16th, with police arresting a man in his 30s or 40s approximately 90 minutes later on suspicion of attempted robbery-murder after he allegedly attacked the woman with a knife and fled with her handbag.
scraped.author: News On Japan
scraped.h1: Woman Dies After Street Stabbing in Tokyo's Nakano
scraped.body_text:
TOKYO - A woman in her 20s was stabbed to death on a residential street near JR Nakano Station in Tokyo on the evening of November 16th, with police arresting a man in his 30s or 40s approximately 90 minutes later on suspicion of attempted robbery-murder after he allegedly attacked the woman with a knife and fled with her handbag.

According to the Metropolitan Police Department, an emergency call was received at around 7:30 p.m. reporting that a woman had been stabbed on a street in Nakano Ward. The victim was found with severe injuries and transported to a hospital in critical condition, where she was later pronounced dead. The attack occurred in a residential neighborhood approximately 200 meters northeast of JR Nakano Station, about a two-minute walk from the station. The surrounding area includes apartment buildings, parks, restaurants and bars, and is frequently used by residents and commuters returning home. Investigators believe the suspect stabbed the woman in the neck with a bladed weapon before stealing her handbag and fleeing the scene. Police launched an extensive investigation, with numerous forensic officers examining the surrounding streets for evidence, including possible footprints. Investigators continued working across a wide area around the crime scene into the night. The suspect was apprehended shortly before 9 p.m. near JR Higashi-Nakano Station, in an area lined with restaurants and other businesses, and was taken into custody under an emergency arrest warrant on suspicion of attempted robbery-murder. Witnesses described a large police operation as officers converged on the location where the man was detained. "About 10 patrol cars suddenly came rushing in, and the doors were already opening while they were still moving," one witness said. "The police officers jumped out and ran straight toward the area in front of them." Photographs taken by witnesses showed several police vehicles gathered near the arrest location, with numerous officers surrounding the suspect. One witness estimated that more than 10 officers were involved in securing the man, who appeared to be around 40 years old. "There were quite a lot of officers surrounding him, probably more than 10," the witness said. Asked whether the man had resisted or acted violently, the witness replied, "No, he didn't." Another witness described the suspect as standing quietly while officers searched his belongings. "The man was just standing there while police officers examined what he had with him," the witness said. "He seemed almost dazed. I would say he was around 40 years old." Residents near the stabbing scene expressed shock that such a violent attack had occurred in a busy neighborhood where pedestrians regularly pass through during the evening. One resident said the street is commonly used as a shortcut by people returning home through the residential district. "There are always a lot of people walking along here because it leads into the residential area," the resident said. Another local resident noted that students from nearby private girls' junior high and high schools also frequently use the street, including during the evening hours. The stabbing has raised concerns about public safety among residents who had considered the neighborhood relatively safe despite its heavy pedestrian traffic. "There are so many people passing through here, but if someone can be stabbed even in a place like this, it's frightening because you never know when you might be in danger," one resident said. Police are also investigating information suggesting that the suspect and the victim may have known each other, raising questions about whether the attack was connected to a personal relationship rather than a random robbery. Investigators are working to establish the circumstances leading up to the stabbing, the relationship between the two individuals and the suspect's motive.

Another witness described the suspect as standing quietly while officers searched his belongings.

"The man was just standing there while police officers examined what he had with him," the witness said. "He seemed almost dazed. I would say he was around 40 years old."

scraped.body_text:
OSAKA - A 30-year-old man known as the "Emperor of Guri-Shita" among young people gathering beneath a popular landmark in Osaka's Dotonbori entertainment district has been arrested on suspicion of sexually assaulting a girl and illegally referring four young people to a demolition contractor in exchange for fees, Osaka Prefectural Police said.

The suspect, Yuya Saito, 30, who has no fixed address and is unemployed, is accused of sexually assaulting a girl and arranging work for four young people, including minors, at a demolition company in Osaka without the required authorization. Police suspect he received referral fees for placing the workers with the company from December 2025 onward. According to investigators, the girl and the four young people had all met Saito at an area commonly known as "Guri-Shita," a gathering place beneath the large Glico running man sign in Dotonbori that has become a popular meeting spot for teenagers and young adults. Saito was reportedly known among those frequenting the area as the "Emperor of Guri-Shita." An acquaintance described Saito as generous toward people in his circle, saying he frequently offered them accommodation, paid for meals and helped those struggling to find employment. "He was a really good person to those close to him. He would let people stay at his place, take everyone out for dinner and pay for everything," the acquaintance said. "If someone didn't have a job, he'd ask whether they wanted to work or come to one of his construction sites." During questioning, Saito reportedly acknowledged receiving money for arranging employment, telling investigators, "I did receive referral fees." Osaka Prefectural Police are continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding the alleged sexual assault and the employment arrangements, including how Saito established relationships with the young people gathering in Dotonbori and the extent of his involvement in placing them with contractors.

items.title: Japan's Supercomputer Hit by Unauthorized Access
items.summary: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer has been temporarily shut down following unauthorized external access to a system used to connect to the facility, raising concerns that user information may have been leaked, the Riken research institute announced on November 16th. (News On Japan)

scraped.title: Japan
scraped.description: Japan
scraped.author: News On Japan
scraped.h1: Japan's Supercomputer Hit by Unauthorized Access
scraped.body_text:
TOKYO - Japan's Fugaku supercomputer has been temporarily shut down following unauthorized external access to a system used to connect to the facility, raising concerns that user information may have been leaked, the Riken research institute announced on November 16th.

According to Riken, which operates Fugaku, the unauthorized access targeted a connection system used by researchers and other users to access the supercomputer. The institute said personal or other user information may have been compromised, although the full extent of the potential data leak remains unclear. Riken has reported the incident to the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, which oversees the institute, and has launched a detailed investigation into the breach. The investigation is examining which parts of the connection system were affected, how long the unauthorized access continued, and whether information was actually leaked. As a precautionary measure, Riken has suspended Fugaku's operations while the investigation continues. The institute has not indicated when the supercomputer will resume service. Fugaku is one of the world's leading supercomputers and has been used extensively for research conducted by government agencies, universities, and other institutions across Japan. The supercomputer plays an important role in supporting advanced scientific research, making the security of its systems and the protection of user information critical to the institutions that rely on its computing capabilities. Fugaku represents the culmination of more than a decade of Japanese investment in high-performance computing, combining advanced domestic processor technology with a national strategy to strengthen scientific research, industrial competitiveness, and technological independence. The supercomputer was developed jointly by Riken and Japanese technology company Fujitsu as the successor to the K computer, which had established Japan as a major force in global supercomputing when it became the world's fastest computer in June 2011. Installed at Riken's research facility in Kobe, Hyogo Prefecture, the K computer was capable of performing more than 10 quadrillion calculations per second and was used for research ranging from earthquake simulations and climate modeling to drug discovery and the development of new materials. Although the K computer was a major technological achievement, advances in computing power and increasingly complex scientific problems prompted the Japanese government to begin planning an even more powerful successor. In December 2013, the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology commissioned Riken to lead the project, and development formally began in April 2014 under the government's Flagship 2020 initiative. The objective was to create a supercomputer capable of handling a much wider range of applications while delivering substantially greater processing power and improved energy efficiency. Rather than simply building a faster version of the K computer, researchers sought to develop a system that could support traditional scientific simulations alongside artificial intelligence, big data analysis, and increasingly sophisticated industrial applications. Fujitsu worked closely with Riken to design the machine's hardware and software, including a new generation of processors specifically optimized for demanding scientific calculations. The resulting A64FX processor was based on the Arm architecture, widely associated with energy-efficient computing, and represented an important departure from the processor technology used in the K computer. The decision was intended to combine high computational performance with relatively low power consumption, a critical consideration for machines containing millions of processing cores. Fugaku ultimately incorporated 158,976 computing nodes and more than 7.6 million processor cores, connected through Fujitsu's high-speed Tofu interconnect network, allowing enormous calculations to be divided among thousands of processors working simultaneously. The system was designed to achieve a theoretical peak performance exceeding 500 quadrillion calculations per second, placing it among the most powerful computing systems ever constructed at the time. The name Fugaku, another name for Mount Fuji, was announced in May 2019 following a public naming competition that attracted 5,181 suggestions. The mountain was chosen as a symbol of both the extraordinary computing performance the machine was expected to achieve and the broad range of scientific and industrial applications it would support. Manufacturing began in 2019, and the first computing racks arrived at Riken's Kobe facility in December of that year. Installation continued through May 2020, following the retirement of the K computer in August 2019. Fugaku's development also coincided with the emergence of the COVID-19 pandemic, creating an unexpected opportunity to demonstrate its capabilities before the machine had officially entered full operation. Beginning in April 2020, Riken made portions of the system available for urgent coronavirus-related research. Researchers used Fugaku to simulate how respiratory droplets and airborne particles spread through indoor environments, including classrooms, offices, trains, and restaurants. The simulations helped illustrate how ventilation, face masks, and seating arrangements could influence the transmission of airborne infections, providing information that contributed to public health discussions during the pandemic. The supercomputer was also used to investigate the behavior of the coronavirus at the molecular level and examine potential treatments, demonstrating its ability to tackle biological problems requiring extremely large numbers of calculations. In June 2020, Fugaku achieved an unprecedented sweep of four major international supercomputing rankings, taking first place in the TOP500 ranking for raw computational performance, HPCG for performance on calculations representative of scientific applications, HPL-AI for artificial intelligence-related computations, and Graph500 for large-scale data processing. Its performance on the TOP500 benchmark reached approximately 416 quadrillion floating-point operations per second, an achievement that placed Japan ahead of competing systems in the United States and China. Subsequent improvements raised the measured performance to approximately 442 quadrillion operations per second. Fugaku retained first place in the TOP500 ranking for four consecutive editions through November 2021, while also holding the leading position across all four major benchmarks during that period. The achievement was particularly significant because supercomputers are generally optimized for particular types of calculations, making it difficult for a single machine to dominate several different performance categories simultaneously. Fugaku was officially completed and opened for shared use on March 9th, 2021, becoming the centerpiece of Japan's High Performance Computing Infrastructure, a national network designed to provide universities, research institutes, and private companies with access to advanced computing resources. Unlike conventional computers, which typically handle calculations through a relatively small number of processors, Fugaku distributes enormous computational tasks across millions of processing cores. This allows scientists to model complicated physical phenomena, analyze massive datasets, and test virtual scenarios that would be impractical or impossible to investigate through conventional experiments alone. The system has been applied to a wide range of scientific challenges, including predicting the effects of earthquakes and tsunamis, simulating typhoons and extreme weather, examining the behavior of new materials, and improving the design of automobiles, aircraft, and energy systems. In medicine, its computing power has supported research into molecular interactions, pharmaceutical compounds, and the behavior of proteins, while in fundamental science it has enabled investigations into the structure of matter and the evolution of the universe. Fugaku's contributions have also received international recognition. Research into the airborne transmission of COVID-19 using the machine received a special Gordon Bell Prize in November 2021, while an international research collaboration using Fugaku won the prestigious Gordon Bell Prize in November 2022. By June 2026, Fugaku had slipped to ninth place in the TOP500 ranking as newer supercomputers in China, the United States, and Europe surpassed its raw processing speed. Nevertheless, it remained one of the world's most capable scientific computing systems, ranking third internationally in the HPCG benchmark, which measures performance on workloads closer to those encountered in practical scientific research. The continued importance of Fugaku reflects the growing role of supercomputers in international technological competition. Governments increasingly regard advanced computing infrastructure as essential not only to scientific discovery but also to economic competitiveness, national security, artificial intelligence development, and the ability to respond to natural disasters and public health emergencies. Japan has already begun preparing for the machine's eventual replacement. In 2025, Riken launched development of a next-generation flagship supercomputer, provisionally named FugakuNEXT, with Fujitsu and U.S. semiconductor company Nvidia participating in the project. The new system, targeted for operation around 2030, is being designed to integrate conventional high-performance scientific computing with advanced artificial intelligence capabilities. Unlike Fugaku, which relies primarily on specially designed central processing units, FugakuNEXT is expected to incorporate graphics processing units to accelerate AI and other computationally demanding workloads. Fujitsu is responsible for the basic design of the overall system and processor components, while Nvidia is contributing technology for the accelerator infrastructure. The project represents another major step in Japan's effort to maintain its position in an increasingly competitive global supercomputing industry. Against this background, the unauthorized access discovered in November 2026 has raised questions about the security of an important part of Japan's national scientific infrastructure. Fugaku supports research involving universities, government institutions, and private companies, making the protection of its computing environment and user information particularly important. Although Riken has not established whether information was actually stolen, the decision to suspend the supercomputer's operations underscores the potential consequences of a security breach affecting a facility that serves as a foundation for some of Japan's most advanced scientific and technological research.
