scraped.title: The capture of Tribune magazine
scraped.author: Jonny Ball
scraped.h1: The capture of Tribune magazine The worker’s rag is now obsessed with Israel
scraped.body_text:
A kind of Left Orientalism exoticizes and fetishizes the icon of the modern guerrilla. (Guy Smallman/Getty)

A kind of Left Orientalism exoticizes and fetishizes the icon of the modern guerrilla. (Guy Smallman/Getty)

In the Fifties, Tribune , the celebrated journal of the Labour Left, announced that “There is a danger of war in the Middle East!”. Plus ça change , we might say now. The region spanning the Eastern Mediterranean and the Gulf has ever been an ethno-religious tinderbox and a resource-rich periphery to the greedy imperial core, rarely a peaceable land. But the editorial continued with a line of argument that feels deeply incongruous today: “Israel may be compelled to fight,” it stated. “Let Socialists see to it that she should have arms to withstand the Arab forces… The cause of Israel is the cause of democratic Socialism.”

Tribune was founded in 1937 by two wealthy socialists, one of whom would later become Chancellor in Attlee’s postwar administration. Its original purpose was to campaign for an anti-fascist, anti-appeasement popular front between Labour and more radical Left parties, including the Communist Party, which at the time was a small but serious outfit with parliamentary representation, cadres of high-minded intellectuals, and many thousands of worker-militants in powerful trade unions. It quickly became a celebrated weekly, publishing George Orwell and the future Labour leader Michael Foot. During the war, it was edited by Nye Bevan, the legendary Welsh miner who went on to found the NHS — and is still a hero of the Labour Left today.

In the 75 years since Tribune ’s editorial, such lofty sentiments with regards to Israel have become unimaginable on the Left. Instead, explicit anti-Zionist postures have become not just fashionable but an essential component of the contemporary progressive identity. “From the River to the Sea” is the Newer Left mantra, an article of faith repeated ad infinitum by those professing an acquaintance with today’s versions of “democratic socialism”. The ability to pursue anti-Israel policy with singular, near-obsessive intensity has become the primary litmus test of one’s political acceptability. Pro-Palestinian activists in Britain have even protested the Left-wing Senator Bernie Sanders for his apparently lackluster displays of fealty to the cause, and their American comrades have taken a similar approach to Zohran Mamdani.

To be sure, an enthusiastic socialist Zionism was bound to falter as the nature of Israel changed: while the Jewish state could be viewed as a David against Arab Goliaths before 1967, the long-running occupations since have flipped the dynamic. Israel is no longer a haven of social-democratic values. Long gone are the socialist celebrations of Israel’s purportedly democratic, collectivist ethos encapsulated by the kibbutzim, the powerful Histadrut , and the construction of a European-style welfare state in a region of familial autocracies. All that is now anathema. Jerusalem embraced the neoliberal turn as thoroughly as Western Europe and the post-Bretton Woods United States. Its politics shifted markedly to the hard-Right, not least as Mizrahi Jews — descendants of those expelled by Arab nationalists across the region — came to wrest political dominance from the generally more liberal-minded, old Ashkenazi elite.

Irrespective of the internal political economy of Israel proper, there are sound, principled reasons for the Left to vigorously oppose ethnic cleansing in the West Bank and the ruthless bombardment of the Gaza Strip. But whatever the actions or political complexion of the Israeli government, it is Zionism itself which is today opposed almost universally on the radical Left. Indeed, according to the implied geographies of “River to the Sea” chanters, and according to the official policy of the Green Party of England and Wales, the mere existence of Israel is held to be the egregious result of a great historical injustice, of “racism”, to be corrected at the first opportunity. It’s not just Israel that has changed, but the Left that has changed too.

By Edward Luttwak

A revamped Tribune , under new ownership, merely echoes this broader trend. The story of the magazine mirrors the sociological and ideological transmutations of Left politics over nearly the last century. Last week, for example, the magazine hosted an event with Andreas Malm — the Swedish academic and author of How to Blow up a Pipeline , who was recently barred from entering the UK — along with Huda Ammori, one of the founders of Palestine Action. It has been suggested that Malm, who appeared at the event via video link, had his permission to enter the UK revoked as a result of his characterization of October 7 as “fundamentally an act of liberation”. In a 2024 essay, he had mused on “the best writings of Islamic Jihad”, the land of Palestine’s “subjugation to fossil [fuel] empire”, and angrily lamented the apparently “real disgrace” that he could not “without equivocation” lend his support to the “armed resistance”. Malm also admits that his initial “cries of jubilation” and screams of “astonishment and joy” on October 7 (all fairly unequivocal) were somewhat tempered by the realization that “they will destroy Gaza. They will kill everyone.”

In this, Malm has been proven prescient. Immediately after news broke of the Hamas-led massacres, anyone even vaguely familiar with the recent and ferocious history of IDF responses to terror attacks correctly predicted that the next phase of conflict would dwarf the scale of any human suffering yet seen in this densely populated strip. But Malm never seems to have conceded that his celebrated “resistance” itself knew full well what the consequences of its actions would be. Nor does he acknowledge that the provocation of a barbarous retaliatory assault was in all likelihood precisely their intention, in order to disrupt the Abraham Accords. The annihilation of Gaza, in the cold calculation of former Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar, was a price worth paying to threaten the gradual but definite lapse in the regional solidarity felt by the powerful sections of the ummah . For rulers residing in the palaces of Gulf petrostates and the region’s martial dictators, a normalization of economic, military and diplomatic relations with Israel took precedence over years of interminable occupation and conflict. Palestine was becoming a mere awkward footnote in the more important considerations of regional realpolitik. In spite of all this, Tribune ’s other worthy guest Ammori started what is now a proscribed organization dedicated to the sabotage of UK military equipment, and has offered adjacent commentary to Malm. Her Palestine Action co-founder told an excitable crowd on 8 October that “the al-Aqsa flood” (Hamas’s preferred term for their most successful pogrom), must be turned “into a tsunami of the whole world”.

So what explains Tribune ’s about-turn, from the enthusiastic Labour Zionism of its genesis towards the most rabid forms of apologia for indiscriminate Islamist terror against civilians (particularly if those civilians happen to be Jews)? It is more than simply the actions of the Israeli government and the IDF. There are ideological double standards at work. The deaths of hundreds of thousands of Tigrayans at the hands of Ethiopian forces in the early 2020s would not have led to wild celebrations at any hypothetical terrorist reprisals against civilians in Addis Ababa.

There are several elements to the story of the Left’s, and Tribune ’s, ideological journey, the first relating directly to the magazine itself, which last year was acquired by Mohamed Ali Harrath. Harrath was a founder of the Tunisian Islamic Front as well as the owner-founder of the Islam Channel. That particular outlet has been censured by Ofcom for broadcasting, among other things, explanations of the precise circumstances in which marital rape and domestic abuse are allowed (“not in a way that damages her eye or damages her tooth or damages her face and makes her ugly”, according to these learned scholars). Harrath, a Sunni Muslim, has also been filmed engaging in outlandish sectarian rants against Shia Muslims. Under such ownership, it’s no wonder that Tribune has departed from its traditional Labourism. But there are broader forces at work. Not least the emergence of a sinister, tacit, de facto alliance between the Left and fundamentalist Islamism — a phenomenon the French philosopher Pierre-André Taguieff identified as Islamo-gauchisme in 2002 but that has only flourished since.

This is a strange political nexus where the most bien pensant , hyper-woke progressive Leftists can find common cause with varying brands of millenarian Shia Islam and militant Sunni jihadism alike. In the Manichean division of the world into oppressed-oppressor, these instances of ultra-conservative religious fanaticism and indiscriminate violence can be coded as the chaotic outbursts and cries of the underdog against a hegemonic capitalist-imperialist world order. This is what allows crowds of Millennial and Gen Z protesters, as well as the aging remnants of the metropolitan Boomer New Left, to mingle on demonstrations with Islamist sympathizers, thinking nothing of celebrating the battlefield victories of groups whose flags are emblazoned with “Curse the Jews” . Yemen’s Houthis may not be perfect, but who are we to condemn their fight in our decadent sham democracy? After all, they alone are resisting Israel’s expansionary, genocidal impulses. Or so the logic goes.

And so along with Tribune , the Left — “The real movement which abolishes the present state of things”, as Marx defined the socialist project — has been transformed. It has morphed from a class-focused, workerist phenomenon, intimately connected to the organized labor movement, into one based on the social justice mantras and worldviews of hordes of over-produced and downwardly mobile graduates, steeped in a woolly language that grasps towards post-colonialism; post-structural critiques of gender, race, “whiteness”; and veneration of the “subaltern” and “Global Majority”. Within the moral framework displayed by these postgraduate foot soldiers, the axioms of today’s Left are not ones of robust universalism, Enlightenment values, or the painstaking work of broad-based coalition-building. That has been superseded by a series of expressively radical poses that delineate membership of the Brahmin Left subculture.

This politics has become the default ideology of a certain social-cultural type — a byproduct of the Blairite expansion of higher education. Its members work almost exclusively in laptop jobs that afford a relative level of autonomy and social prestige if not particularly large remuneration packages. Because of this, and the fact that they struggle to step onto the housing ladder before they inherit their parents’ real estate asset wealth, they think of themselves as unfairly proletarianized. Even so, they identify themselves through a certain style of trendy clothes and the renting of extortionately priced rooms in gentrifying enclaves of urban Britain where old copies of Why I’m No Longer Talking to White People About Race sit next to Ikea house plants. The more politically literate have a pile of Verso tomes . They carry tote bags, read Sally Rooney, and watch obscure Mubi documentaries. They acknowledge “lived experience”, mental health and “emotional labor”. They are converts to a distinct creed of extremely online Millennial and Gen Z socialism that produces little to nothing by way of workplace struggles, institutional power, face-to-face associational culture, or grassroots community activism. Their political economy is broad and inchoate, but they know that Palestine must be free, that trans women are women, that there’s a button in the Treasury that says “wealth tax” that wicked neoliberals refuse to press, that Britain needs its own Black Lives Matter, and that oil must be stopped — today. Among the public intellectuals and discourse-generators that give a sort of cultural-political coherence to this caste, a brand of anti-Western “anti-imperialism” predominates. It rarely cares to condemn the geopolitical ambitions of Moscow, say, or Tehran. Meanwhile, Israel, a country of 10 million, 2,000 miles away, is cast as the crux around which world politics somehow revolves, the prime mover for domestic political mobilization, apparently the sine qua non of something they call “late-stage” capitalism — more in hope than expectation.

By Jonny Ball

And it’s this Third Worldist, anti-Western outlook — along with the moral and cultural relativism that flows from the demands of radical deconstruction prevalent in the academy — that permits support for suicide bombings, the subjugation of women, the imposition of Sharia law and open antisemitism. All this is apparently acceptable as long as it’s done in pursuit of Israel’s ultimate defeat, the destruction of the “white settler colonial” entity par excellence in its entirety, not simply a withdrawal to pre-1967 borders. At home, antisemitism is easy enough to dismiss as a nefarious, deliberate distraction from the real work of “opposing genocide”. Since racism, in the Brahmin Left’s pseudo-Marxist reading, must manifest itself as structural (i.e. appearing in institutional discrimination and negative, divergent social outcomes for ethnic groups), then Jew-hatred can be classified as a mere individual prejudice, not nearly on a par with anti-black racism, or, God forbid, Islamophobia. Indeed, a lingering view of antisemitism as a “punching up” phenomenon remains; it’s considered an understandable if unseemly by-product of systematic oppression by Jews, or by a powerful elite in which Jews are over-represented, confirming the continued validity of the old social democrat August Bebel’s assertion that antisemitism was “the socialism of fools”. This socialism is alive and well. And so the same people who talk about “micro-aggressions”, “unconscious bias” and calls to “decolonize” racist curricula will excuse Islamist death squads against Jewish civilians.

After 20 years of wage suppression, squeezed household budgets, the deterioration of the public realm, the accentuation of housing crises, gaping regional inequalities, anemic growth and secular decline at home, the British Left has landed on Israel-Palestine as the most successful rallying cry it can now muster. Industrial militancy may be all-but dead, but at least the Middle East still gets the new adherents onto the streets. Never mind the fact that London, unlike Washington, now exercises little-to-no influence over the Middle East, or that Israel’s onslaught against the Palestinians would have played out identically even if Zack Polanski himself had been the British Prime Minister.

This kind of monomaniacal, post-imperial obsession with the Holy Land is the end product of a political movement that has lost its social foundations. The Left’s old institutional networks in the unions, working-men’s clubs and mass parties once buttressed a level of broad popular support and a political grounding among ordinary working people in Britain — but those networks have decayed. Detached, incubating itself almost purely in seminar rooms and online, and relegating itself into subcultural status ever more forcefully, much of the Left has retreated into the politics of cultural signaling and moral performance, abandoning any serious ambition to acquire or exercise power, much less any ambitions to represent and articulate the aspirations of the working class.

On the Brahmin Left, zeitgeisty causes célèbres appear and disappear with dizzying frequency — and they are rarely the same causes that animate much of the country at large. Meanwhile, a kind of Left Orientalism exoticizes and fetishizes the icon of the modern guerrilla, ascribing virtues to foreign actors whom British Leftists would find abominable if they had any power or proximity to them at home. The uncoupling of the once-great Tribune from its roots and traditions is a symptom of this political degradation. It is a remarkable journey from Bevan to Hamas, and not one that the old Tribune would have recognized.

Jonny Ball is a Contributing Editor at UnHerd . He formerly wrote under the name Despotic Inroad.

scraped.title: The Noughties’ naked sexism
scraped.author: Terri White
scraped.h1: What men’s magazines did to sex They pornified Western culture
scraped.body_text:
“By the time “Nuts” was selling a few-hundred-thousand copies a week, magazine racks looked like a warzone littered with women’s naked bodies”. (Mick Hutson/Getty)

“By the time “Nuts” was selling a few-hundred-thousand copies a week, magazine racks looked like a warzone littered with women’s naked bodies”. (Mick Hutson/Getty)

It wasn’t so much the straw that broke the camel’s back as the rope. Rough manila rope to be specific: about an inch and a half in diameter, looped around my neck. It was 2016, and my cool-ass liberal views on pornography and sex were shaky at best, the night my boyfriend picked up the ends and pulled hard. My airway cut off, black bled into my peripheral vision. He pulled again, harder. Tiny white stars burst in the darkness, a throbbing drum beat filling my ears as blood bound for my brain stopped dead.

As I gasped — well, tried to — in blind-panic and mock-excitement, I couldn’t help but wonder… was this empowerment ? Was this where a decade and half of choice feminism had got me? And, well, it’s precisely where. Saying “yes” as he strangled me so hard that spiral-groove abrasions crawled down my throat afterwards. But then, this night on my back and entirely in his hand scared me sane, was the hinge of my sexual politics.

A decade prior, in 2006, I was a committed choice feminist (we should support any-and-all choices a woman makes, including those for the pleasure and profit of men), and a senior editor on men’s weekly magazine Nuts (see previous brackets). A decade on, in 2026, I’m an anti-porn radical feminist, surveying where two-plus decades of choice feminism — and its rabid little sister, pick-me feminism (we should support any-and-all choices a woman makes, unless it obstructs the pleasure and profit of men) — has got us as a society.

By Polly Clark

Put simply: men have women, more than ever, by the throat. Regardless of the straws one high-profile conviction has us grasping, we’re still up to our necks in the conditions and culture I helped to create in the Noughties. It’s a culture that enabled men like Russell Brand, in which they could act out the misogyny they ceaselessly “bantered” about, while women like me cheered them on from the sidelines, standing on the backs of our sisters to get a better view.

It’s worth saying that I expect to be accused of bad-faith bandwagon-jumping. I’ve written about my two-and-a-half years at Nuts just twice before: in a play about rape culture, and, journalistically, in a Left-leaning newspaper . The latter: an examination of the damage we’d done to the (largely working-class) young women who appeared in the magazine, the damage I’d done as a young working-class woman.

My naked (certainly naive) honesty, admitting that I’d been seeking a permanent path out of my own financial precarity through the exploitation of others, was met with intellectualized disgust. The readers — middle-and-upper-class-Left — decided I was a moron, a liar, a woman faking a mea culpa , hungry for attention (of course!).

My gears were ground to dust by those for whom the poverty I spent my early years in was a coked-up dinner-party point-of-order. And I was baffled. Wasn’t I attempting to hold myself accountable? But then, I was starting down the path of rejecting liberal feminism. I was the enemy who one day would be back to try and take their porn (correct! Ding ding!).

Their disdain wasn’t just hacked up for me though; they had plenty left for the young women in Nuts (who, apparently, were also idiots). And they certainly didn’t think any better of the uneducated working-class men they assumed exclusively bought the magazine. But then, they didn’t know what I did. What made Nuts so powerful, so dangerous.

The readers weren’t just white-van-driving blokes from council estates, but all men ( Nuts sold over 100 million copies over its lifetime), with a particularly strong showing among middle-class boys. The office regularly fielded complaints from teachers at very good schools in very nice areas whose classrooms were being flooded with it.

And these are the boys who concern me the most. The generation — now in their thirties, running companies, setting standards, raising sons and daughters of their own — made men not just by magazines that made soft-porn the wallpaper of their lives, but by a culture that was soaked in aggressive sexism.

***

The Nineties closed out with a 16-year-old Britney Spears on that pedophile-fluffing cover of Rolling Stone , and with FHM projecting a nude picture of 21-year-old Gail Porter onto the Houses of Parliament without her knowledge or consent. And, just like that, as the Noughties began, the gates of misogyny were flung wide open.

Live on BBC Radio 1, Chris Moyles offered to “take” 15-year-old Charlotte Church’s virginity when she passed the age of consent. Kylie and Geri Halliwell copped-off for a gleeful Chris Evans on TFI Friday . A female audience member was groped on stage at a Johnny Vegas stand-up show. Russell Brand and Noel Fielding joked about being rapists alongside a stone-faced Lily Allen on Channel 4’s The Big Fat Quiz of the Year . Indie lad-band The Pigeon Detectives sang about knocking women about (“You’re hurt cause I hit you/ But we know it’s only a game/ You said I make you walk into a door/ But I can’t control myself.”)

A hyper-sexist, hyper-sexualizing culture that turned women and girls into hollowed-out things to be leered at and, ultimately, fucked , was unleashed. Exploitation was conflated with consent, objectification and degradation celebrated, complaints from radical feminists (who rightly pointed out how misogyny can never be divorced from the material reality of women’s lives) deflected with supposed-celebrations of female agency and freedom ( miserable bitches just needed to lighten up, right! ).

If you joke about being a sexist pig, a rapist — you can’t be a sexist pig, an actual rapist, right? That was the argument, and one that gifted men, sexist pigs, and rapists like Russell Brand, unfettered access to women’s bodies.

There’s no two ways about it: objectifying women was hugely profitable for all concerned in the Noughties. Though initially, we didn’t realize this at the magazine.

Nuts — one of the biggest ever magazine launches from IPC Media, publishers of NME , Marie Claire and Horse & Hound — landed in January 2004 (a week before rival Zoo , developed under the codename Project Tyson; yes, after the boxer and convicted rapist ).

I was deputy news editor, our glossy pages filled with girls, crime, jokes, sport and cars — but not nipples, which were banned. After all, we’d say, “it’s the magazine fathers and sons can read together”. On the cover of that first issue — of which one million copies were given away — stood, in a gym-appropriate vest, model and fitness pro Nell McAndrew.

Promotion was via a massive £8 million advertising budget: a large chunk spent on TV ads showing women spooning DIY while their blokes read the magazine. “Women!” boomed the voiceover while the theme from The Great Escape played. “Don’t expect any help on a Thursday!” This slice of regressive sexism aired to millions during an ad break in the final series of Friends on Channel 4.

Early covers starred Beyonce in a denim skirt, Britney in a bikini, J-Lo in lingerie, before men in focus groups told us (shockingly!) that they actually wanted to see nipples. Specifically, British nipples. And so, celebrities were replaced with glamour models. Until, they said, they actually wanted to see “real” British nipples, those attached to the girls from their hometown, the pub, the office. Girls that might, on the right night, laugh at their jokes and, ultimately, shag them.

It was, it became clear, about proximity, access, attainability. And so, to unleash those extra sales (and profits), breasts and nipples were in (or should I say, out), as were “real girls”. These overwhelmingly working-class girls were now the stars of Nuts (but not sharing in the profits; they weren’t paid, taking their own pictures and sending them in, unlike the professional models making tens of thousands).

At the same time, the ideas for “real girl” features — which I became responsible for after being promoted to features editor and then associate editor, number three on the magazine — became increasingly porn-coded. The covers screamed “Britain’s Sexiest Secretaries!”; “Topless For the First Time!”; “Girls With Girls!”; “Babes Go Topless Together!”; eventually devolving into “100 Big Boobed Girls!”, “The Giant Boobs Issue!’, and “VERY BIG BOOBS!”. Literacy and brain cells were shed as quickly as the women’s clothes.

But readers didn’t just want access to the girls, they wanted to know what to do with them. So, we dialed-up the magazine’s sex content with “confessions”, “advice” and “tips”. “Naughty sex guaranteed!” read one cover line; “Turn good girls bad!” promised another. We were careful not to breach consent in the articles, but it was more assumed than sought. And while practices like strangulation were off-limits, I ghosted columns about anal, deep-throating, tit-wanks. One sex tip I remember editing said simply: “Treat me rough!”. Girls, in our world, were gagging for it, always. Willing to act out every fantasy and make it reality.

Before Nuts and Zoo , naked pictures of “up for it” women were packaged in the magazines sold in newsagents from the top-shelf. Pornography was clearly labeled and ring-fenced as such. But by the time Nuts was selling a few-hundred-thousand copies a week, magazine racks looked like a warzone littered with women’s naked bodies, their faces fixed and unsmiling. Going into Tesco for a meal deal suddenly felt like staring into an abyss. Flesh-and-blood women and girls were assaulted by acres of flayed female flesh. Dehumanized images reflected back at them, at us, at me. We were all stripped bare of dignity and personhood, whether we took our clothes off or not. It was an experience I knew too well.

***

Another night, this time when I was still at primary school. My mum was working as a barmaid in town, her boyfriend calling me into their bedroom, where he sat naked. In one hand, his penis; in the other, a pornographic magazine (of the Fiesta, Escort kind).

He told me to sit down, pushed the open magazine towards me. Across the double-page spread, a woman — big breasts, tiny waist — on her back. Her legs spread wide, tangled hair shooting from the darkness. Another, on all fours, held together by a staple.

“Hold it up”, he demanded, beginning to move his hand up and down. I complied, holding it over my eyes. “Lower,” he barked. He needed to see my humiliation to get off. There was no escape — not for me, not for them. We were bound together in an unholy covenant of degradation. I saw these women in the real girls in Nuts , reduced to one use: facilitating the orgasm of men.

Any argument against this was destroyed on another night, when I sat in the Nuts office uploading 100-plus pictures of topless women, before digitally decapitating them for a new website called “Assess My Breasts”. The name of the “game”: men ranking every pair out 10. But, to protect the women’s “dignity” (the argument went), we’d remove their heads, their identities, leaving just a disembodied pair of tits. It felt like a tacit admission of how little anything else mattered.

By Kathleen Stock

The internet broke both me that night, and Nuts itself eventually. As the Noughties ticked into the 2010s, our new tech (phones) and new methods of distribution (the internet) meant that pornography could be easily accessed by pretty much everyone, everywhere, at any time, for free.

It became the air we breathe, and the crucial role Nuts played in pornifying our culture for this step-change is clear. We made “soft” porn mainstream, and left the door wide open for the extreme stuff to slip into its places. By 2010, 88% of porn involved “physical aggression” like “spanking, gagging, and slapping”.

“Pornography is a celebration of rape and injury to women,” wrote Andrea Dworkin. And who can look at modern porn — hair-pulling, face-spitting, rough anal, double-penetration, choking, “gangbangs” — and not agree with those words? And so, when pornography is mainstream, the celebration of rape and injury to women is too. The acts on screen bleed into acts in the real world.

These days, in fact, it seems we only reserve shame for women who say no. To being strangled. To anal. To threesomes. Who have a problem, like one of Brand’s victims, with having their breasts grabbed in public.

We need to radically overhaul the culture we’ve built brick-by-brick over the last two-plus decades. And the path back begins with de-pornifying the culture we corrupted so thoroughly. We don’t need to teach men and boys what consent is ( please! ), but we do need to remind them that ignoring it, forcing your way through it, has dire consequences. And say, forcefully, that women and girls are more than a pair or tits. Or a mouth, a vagina, an anus. “Tarts” for men’s pleasure. Russell Brand’s been told that in no uncertain terms — now we need all men and boys to hear that too.

Terri White is an author, documentarian, and culture and social affairs journalist.

scraped.title: Reality Isn't What It Used To Be...
scraped.description: ZeroHedge - On a long enough timeline, the survival rate for everyone drops to zero
scraped.author: Tyler Durden
scraped.h1: Reality Isn't What It Used To Be...
scraped.body_text:
Authored by James Howard Kunstler via Kunstler.com ,

"America has now shifted beyond ordinary political quarreling and into the dark territory of a real constitutional crisis."

- Jeff Childers

Reality isn't what it used to be: a baseline consensus about what is actually happening and what it means. All you know is something seems to be up, but what is that something? And what is it up to? Nobody really knows. Whatever it is, it's getting people to strip the Costco stores of canned ravioli and toilet paper.

One thing agreed upon: the president has made himself scarce the past several days. And top cabinet officials - Bessent, Rubio, Blanche, plus COS Miller - were spirited away to regional military bases for safe-keeping. . . the Veep hiding out at Camp David. . . rumors of an Iranian drone plot to kill them all. . . maybe involving terrorist cells implanted here during "Joe Biden's" four-year migrant orgy. (How did we let that happen?)

One module of this disabled reality function is the suspicion that a certain cohort in American politics wants to destroy the USA and is using the Democratic Party to carry it out. The midterm election was the device to boost them up to power, and it seemed to work, maybe a little too well. Their poobahs in Congress are in full gloat-and-sneer mode, promising that the beatings will continue until morale improves, yuk, yuk. The preposterous Cherokee maiden Elizabeth Warren was just instructed by federal attorneys to preserve her records - after shooting off her mouth about using her chair on the Senate Banking Committee to destroy Trump adjutants.

For all the faults of our reality cognition, it's hard to imagine that the president and his trusted colleagues did not see election shenanigans coming from a thousand miles away, especially military intelligence. Do you suppose they haven't been surveying the scene all year? The election numbers only add up if you use the "new maff." James Talarico actually elected in Texas? I'm sure.

The DNI, one Jay Clayton, is obliged to report on election doings five days before Christmas. Maybe trim the tree with a bandolier of .270 Winchester rounds and spiff up the Tikka T3X Superlite bolt action. Wonder what the CIA will tell Mr. Clayton. They've been in rather a bad odor since blowing JFK's head off in 1963. Half the country thinks if anyone queered the election it was them. Personally, I believe they merely assisted in the operation.

But, of course, the whole point of the in-your-face election steal with such a garish outcome was exactly to prompt the Trump admin to respond , to lay out the case, to flop it all out on the table like so much raw meat. . . and see what happens. (Watch the animals instinctively snatch the meat.) The "our democracy" animals have been telling you for months exactly what they aim to do: incite a mass freak-out of their mentally-ill myrmidons in the streets, followed by grandiose declarations that the country is now in the hands of their favorite governors (Newsom, Pritzker, Hochul, Healey, Kotek, Hobbs, Spammy). I can't wait for them to try that.

Meanwhile, there is that unfinished business in Iran. Those autumn weeks ramping up into the midterm, it was absolutely obvious that Mr. Trump would refrain from any new action. The sedition-minded news media had softened up the public's already deranged faculties with narratives of swelling anti-war fever, so they could pin the election outcome on it. It was a fiasco, they said. The nation voted against it! We lost the war! Blah blah.

You were supposed to forget about Iran's nuclear jihad - by voting for jihad inside the USA. In our very Congress! As Homey D. Clown always said, I don't think so . Iran was rooting for a Democratic Party triumph , from which you can infer they think the Democratic Party is down with jihad - which appears to be so, since their DSA branch won 8 House seats, and go ahead and count Abdul El-Sayed on their team in the Senate, too, however he pretends to be the reincarnation of Jimmy Stewart going to Washington.

The president himself pointed out that the other Persian Gulf nations begged him to back off Iran, because Iran threatened to wipe out their vital infrastructure: oil refineries and terminals, de-sal plants, airports. Iran could brag on that through September and October, knowing the USA would stand off anyway. Now, things have changed.

Looks like the IRGC didn't plan how things might play after the election. You might surmise that Trump, Rubio, Hegseth and Company are a little weary of getting jerked around by these shifty maniacs. You could also suppose that the blockade is chipping away at the IRGC's infamous fortitude - no paychecks for the troops, and anyway, their money is worthless. Can't buy anything, and nothing to buy it with even if you tried. Must be getting a little uncomfortable over there, and we all know the restless spirit that possesses hungry people.

Also meanwhile, things in-country here have also gone wonky, a little bit. First, Microsoft's cloud network crashed for two days , putting the schnitz on businesses, hospitals, public utilities, and governments that run MS's notoriously janky products. Then you got the nationwide air service "ground stop," a first-order clusterfuck, hundreds of thousands stranded at airports, fuggeddabowt going to sleep, getting any dinner - not to mention scaring the bejeezus out of anyone with a memory of 9/11. So far, a faulty router in Arkansas is the assigned culprit. Was it really about that? Or are they rubbing more KY-Jelly onto an already slippery reality?

On Tuesday, Nov. 17, at 2:20 p.m. Eastern time, the govt aims to test its Emergency Alert System. TVs and cable broadcasters, satellite providers will shriek for about one minute, sending the poorly-informed under their desks and into broom closets.

Looks like a heckuva week upcoming. Trump, Putin, and Xi meet up Thursday in Shenzhen, China. That will occupy the foreground while events whirl in the background. Can any of it bring us closer to an agreement, at least, about what is real and what is not?

scraped.title: "They Are F**king Terrified": White House Demands Sign-Off Before Any Federal Employee Testifies To Congress
scraped.description: ZeroHedge - On a long enough timeline, the survival rate for everyone drops to zero
scraped.author: Tyler Durden
scraped.h1: "They Are F**king Terrified": White House Demands Sign-Off Before Any Federal Employee Testifies To Congress
scraped.body_text:
The White House has told every executive branch agency that no employee may agree to appear before a congressional committee until White House Counsel Will Scharf's office and the legislative affairs team sign off , according to a memo Scharf issued Monday that was obtained by Axios .

The memo orders agencies to follow "the established White House consultation process ... before any agency personnel may agree to appear before any congressional committee." It comes seven weeks before Democrats take control of both the House and the Senate in January, with investigations of the administration already lined up.

Scharf's office will apply its own reading of what counts as a "legitimate" inquiry when it decides whether an agency employee gets to testify . A White House official told Axios that reasonable requests will be honored and the rest turned away. "The Trump administration will not be extorted, intimidated, or threatened into submission by politically motivated baseless investigations," the official said.

Democratic strategist Justin Snyder reacted to the memo on X: "Holy shit. They are fucking TERRIFIED."

Holy shit. They are fucking TERRIFIED. https://t.co/MHlxfUUr0j

— Justin Snyder || TheMaineWonk (@TheMaineWonk) November 16, 2026

The memo follows a letter Scharf sent on Nov. 9 to Rep. Robert Garcia (D-CA), who takes over the House Oversight Committee in January. "Congressional investigations must further a legitimate legislative task; Congress cannot employ them to exercise powers of criminal prosecution assigned to the Executive and the Judiciary," Scharf wrote, before warning that "process designed merely to abuse or instill fear in the recipient may cross the line into blatant criminality."

The letter quotes Democratic Rep. Emily Randall promising to pass out subpoenas "like candy," Rep. Analilia Mejia vowing to toss them out "like Mardi Gras beads," and Sen. Ed Markey joking about needing "new forests" for the paper. It cites Garcia's "LAWYER UP" campaign, launched on election night , and accuses him of chalking up his motives to "gay" "pettiness" rather than any legislative purpose , a reference to remarks he made at Crooked Con.

Garcia, who said on Nov. 10 that his committee is weighing a probe of former chief of staff Susie Wiles , shot back that Congress' investigative powers don't need the "permission of the White House," and that "it appears Donald Trump has something to hide," NBC reported .

Attorney General Todd Blanche has declined to rule out prosecuting Democratic lawmakers who investigate Trump officials, as we reported , and on Sunday US Attorney Aaron Reitz sent Sen. Elizabeth Warren a demand to preserve every record tied to her planned investigations. scraped.title: Mamdani Disbands NYPD’s Elite Crowd Control Unit, Creates Civilian-led Team ‘Without Weapons or Arrest Powers’ to Respond to Riots › American Greatness
scraped.description: The overhaul bans specific crowd control tactics such as tear gas, pepper spray, and kettling.
scraped.h1: Mamdani Disbands NYPD’s Elite Crowd Control Unit, Creates Civilian-led Team ‘Without Weapons or Arrest Powers’ to Respond to Riots
scraped.body_text:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced Monday that he is disbanding the New York Police Department’s Strategic Response Group (SRG), gutting the NYPD’s crowd control abilities during protests and riots.

In a video statement, Monday, the Democrat Socialist mayor said that the unit’s counterterrorism functions will be consolidated into the NYPD’s Intelligence and Counterterrorism Bureau, while a toothless civilian-led “Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division (CDDD)” will handle violent protests.

“During our campaign, I promised New Yorkers that we would disband the Strategic Response Group and separate counterterrorism from protest response, and today we are delivering on that promise,” Mamdani stated.

The CDDD will be housed within the Mayor’s Office of Community Safety, and will consist of unarmed leftists without arrest powers. As the unit is not expected to be fully operational until 2028, the NYPD in the interim will deploy the brand new “First Amendment Support Team (FAST),” a 30-officer unit reportedly trained in de-escalation that operates within the NYPD’s Community Affairs Bureau.

As part of the overhaul, crucial crowd control tactics will be banned, such as tear gas, pepper spray, and kettling. Additionally, law enforcement will not be allowed to carry long guns during demonstrations and “long-range acoustic devices” will be limited to 90 decibels.

“We are creating a Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division within the Mayor’s Office of Community Safety to prepare for and respond to protests through dialogue and engagement,” Mamdani stated. “This will not be a uniformed police unit, it will be made up of civilians—without weapons or arrest powers.”

The mayor made the announcement while standing alongside City Council member Chi Ossé, a fellow DSA member and ally who was arrested twice while protesting in 2026.

“Trained officers can be called upon to make arrests—including those who engage in civil disobedience,” Mamdani said, turning to Ossé and adding cheerfully: “we both know something about that.”

Ossé was arrested first in April while attempting to block an eviction in Bedford-Stuyvesant and again in September while protesting in front of the United Nations ahead of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s speech.

He was one of four people arrested and charged with obstruction of governmental administration and disorderly conduct on April 22, 2026.

The far-left councilmember was also among the over 100 unruly pro-Palestinian agitators arrested outside the UN on September 24. Over a thousand pro-Palestinian activists marched through NYC that day to protest Netanyahu’s speech at the UN General Assembly.

The Marxist mayor has repeatedly called Netanyahu a “war criminal” who is “not welcome in New York City.”

Mamdani himself has been arrested multiple times for civil disobedience, including an incident in 2023 when he was taken into custody for disorderly conduct after leading a protest that blocked traffic outside Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer’s (D-N.Y.) home in Brooklyn.

“New Yorkers exercising their constitutional right to protest should not be met with the same police response as a terrorism threat. We are establishing a new, civilian-led approach that prioritizes dialogue, engagement and de-escalation,” he stated.

Police Benevolent Association President Patrick Hendry, who represents more than 21,000 New York City police officers, released a fiery statement Monday condemning the move.

“Today is not a good day for New Yorkers who just want a safe and orderly city. Mayor Mamdani is showing his true colors: he’s willing to put your safety and police officers’ safety at risk to appease his radical base,” Hendry posted on X. “So the next time your life is disrupted by demonstrators who are blocking bridges and roadways or causing chaos on our streets, remember: Mayor Mamdani is on their side, not yours.”

Scott Munro, the president of the NYPD’s detectives’ union, also expressed concern Monday about the mayor’s decision to disband the SRG.

“Disbanding this vital unit proves just how disconnected City Hall is from the realities of policing New York City,” Munro said in a statement posted on X.

With diminished crowd control capabilities, NYPD detectives will now be pulled away from investigating crimes and seeking justice for victims to help police the hundreds of protests across our city. That’s not making New Yorkers safer.

The mayor and elected officials applauding this decision need to remember: They’re no longer standing on a protest line. They’re responsible for leading a city. It’s time they started acting like it.

According to the NYPD website, the SRG was set up to respond to “citywide mobilizations, civil disorders, and major events with highly trained personnel and specialized equipment. They are also deployed to areas requiring an increased police presence due to increased crime or other conditions. With multiple missions that include disorder response, crime suppression, and crowd control, SRG has proven to be a critical asset during events like parades, protests, and the papal visit. SRG also mobilizes for shootings, bank robberies, missing persons, demonstrations, or other significant incidents.”

scraped.h1: Trump to Meet With Putin and Xi at First-Ever Trilateral Summit in China–May Also Meet With Kim Jong Un
scraped.body_text:
President Donald Trump departed the White House Monday, to begin a multi-day trip to Asia that includes the first-ever trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump said this morning that he may also meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his visit to China later this week.

“We’ll be with President Xi. He was here a month ago, and we’re also going to meet with President Putin, and we may meet with Kim Jong Un also. So that’ll be good. We have a chance to accomplish a lot,” Trump told reporters as he left the White House.

The president is traveling this week to Manila, Philippines and Shenzhen, China, for a pair of summits to discuss nuclear disarmament issues and the war with Iran.

On the first leg of the trip, Trump will meet with the “Quad” allies (Japan, India, Australia) in the Philippines, where he is expected to sign a trade deal with Thailand and address Southeast Asian concerns regarding China’s regional aggression.

The summit in Shenzhen later in the week will reportedly focus on nuclear stockpile reduction, the war in Iran, and potentially Russia’s war in Ukraine, marking the first time the leaders of the U.S., China, and Russia have met together.

A senior White House official told reporters on Friday that there were “no plans at all for engagement with North Korea,” though Trump said back in August that he would try to meet with Kim Jong Un this year to reengage on nuclear issues.

The president met with Kim several times during his first term in office, including in 2019 when Trump became the first sitting U.S. president to step inside North Korea at the Korean Demilitarized Zone.

The U.S. delegation on Air Force One includes Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett, and Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino.

Trillionaire Elon Musk will join the delegation for the China leg of the trip, traveling as an advisor given his business interests in the U.S.–China relationship. He will not participate in the trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin or the bilateral Trump–Xi session, officials said.

Notably absent is former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who accompanied Trump to China in May but resigned last week amid the alleged Chinese-spy affair scandal.

scraped.h1: U.S. Universities See Steep Decline in Enrollment by International Students
scraped.body_text:
New international student enrollment at U.S. universities fell by 15 percent this fall, according to a survey of more than 800 universities released by the Institute of International Education.

Politico reports the Trump administration’s tighter visa restrictions, stricter vetting and visa interview and appointment bottlenecks are contributing to a noticeable decline in international student enrollment nationwide this fall.

The visa crackdown is accomplishing two administration goals, narrowing avenues of potential immigration and hitting the bank accounts of academic institutions conservatives have long criticized.

Data released in November 2026 by the Institute of International Education , based on a survey of more than 800 U.S. institutions, highlights a sustained downward trend with first-time international student enrollments dropping 15 percent in fall 2026 after plunging 18 percent in fall 2025.

According to the NY Times , total international student numbers dropped 9 percent in fall 2026, compounding a 3 percent decline from the prior year as education leaders noted an unusual uptick in already-enrolled students leaving their U.S. programs before graduation due to heightened uncertainty.

The trend of declining international students has prompted some higher education leaders to speak out.

Michael Roth, president of Wesleyan University, a private liberal arts school, told Politico:

This is great for the United States that they’re spending money here, that they’re learning about our culture and our country. To just make it harder in the name of some kind of nationalism, it seems like we’re shooting ourselves in the foot just to see how good our boots are.

Benjamin Johnson, a spokesperson for Ohio State, said the university’s international student enrollment “strengthens the academic experience” for all of their students, adding, “We want the world’s best and brightest to choose Ohio State for school and stay to build a life and career in Ohio.”

Because international students frequently pay full tuition, their absence has created immediate budget shortfalls across American higher education.

A State Department spokesperson said in a statement that the administration is “protecting our nation and our citizens by upholding the highest standards of national security and public safety through our visa process. As Secretary [Marco] Rubio said, ‘a visa is a privilege, not a right.’”

The unnamed spokesperson added, “The United States continues to welcome qualified international students whose academic pursuits contribute to American colleges and universities, support the U.S. economy, and strengthen our nation’s global competitiveness.”

'The victim also disclosed that there was a 'rule' in the house, and the rule was not to tell anyone what was happening in the household, or they would get in trouble.'

According to the affidavit, a child was placed in the couple's home between Sept. 20, 2021, and March 9, 2022.

WTSP, citing the affidavit, said the child told investigators that Borsuk and Ballard repeatedly made the child engage in inappropriate sexual contact — "sometimes nearly every day."

Citing authorities, WFLA-TV reported that Borsuk and Ballard allegedly called the child into their bedroom and made him lie naked in bed with them while touching the victim inappropriately.

"The victim also disclosed that there was a 'rule' in the house, and the rule was not to tell anyone what was happening in the household, or they would get in trouble," the affidavit said, according to WFLA.

RELATED: Dad who fostered about 20 children caught with child porn while leaving cruise with pregnant wife, kids: Affidavit

Sheriff Bob Gualtieri said Borsuk and Ballard fostered 23 boys between 2017 and 2023 and adopted five boys between 2015 and 2023.

WFLA, citing the newly released arrest affidavit, said both Ballard and Borsuk were arrested Nov. 5 on the molestation charge.

What's more, Ballard was arrested for child porn possession and bestiality charges only a few months ago.

Blaze News previously reported that Ballard on June 17 was arrested and charged with 20 counts of possession of child pornography and five counts of sexual activity involving animals.

The sheriff's office said in a June statement that detectives received a tip from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children that a "person was communicating on the app 'Kik' and disclosing he was sexually abusing his 7-year-old son."

Detectives identified Ballard as the suspect, and police said a search was conducted on his cellphone.

"Dozens of child pornography videos of children between the ages of infancy and eleven years old, and five videos depicting sexual acts between people and animals were discovered," the sheriff's office stated.

At the time of Ballard's arrest, four adoptive children were living in the couple's home.

Sheriff Gualtieri said at a June press conference, "This is really a very difficult case because it involves the betrayal of the trust that the child welfare system puts into people who volunteer to help the most vulnerable among us; and those are children who have been abused, abandoned, and neglected."

The sheriff's office told Blaze News that Ballard was released on a surety bond on Aug. 18 following his June arrest and then rearrested on the new charge Nov. 5. Both Ballard and Borsuk remained behind bars Monday, jail records indicate.

What's more, Ballard and Borsuk co-wrote a book titled "Our Journey: A collection of moments that make a lifetime," self-described as a "living record of the love that knows no boundaries and the incredible story of building a family through the extraordinary gift of adoption."

scraped.h1: Liberal bias of Grammy Awards is on full display in this year's nominations
scraped.body_text:
The Grammy nominations include some far-left nods.

Michelle Obama received her third Grammy nomination on Monday, and the committee also gave a nod for an anti-Trump protest song.

Obama is nominated in the Best Audio Book, Narration, and Storytelling Recording category for the audio version of her 2025 fashion and style book titled "The Look."

The 'No Kings' song shares the name of the liberal protests against President Donald Trump and his policies.

The protest song "No Kings" by Jesse Welles and featuring Joan Baez also got a nomination in the Best American Roots Performance category.

Welles is known for injecting political satire into his songs such as "Join ICE," which mocks the people joining Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

"Take my advice, if you're lacking control and authority, come with me and hunt down minorities, join ICE!" he sings.

The "No Kings" song shares the name of the liberal protests against President Donald Trump and his policies. The lyrics read , "No hatred, no violence, no starvation, and no greed, and no kings, no kings, no kings."

Baez has previously expressed her left-wing beliefs. In 2012, she contributed to the Occupy Wall Street benefit album, which was another far-left protest.

"What's needed is an anthem, something that everybody can sing. They don't have to worry about all the verses. Just sing the 'no kings, no kings, no kings' part," the 85-year-old previously said of Welles' song.

Michelle Obama had been nominated for a Grammy twice before and won both times. In 2024 she won for "The Light We Carry: Overcoming In Uncertain Times" in the audio book category and in 2020 for "Becoming" under the category's previous name, Best Spoken Word Album.

RELATED: The Obamas release a statement about Harvey Weinstein, but there's something missing

The 69th annual Grammy awards ceremony will be held on Feb. 7, 2027, in Los Angeles, California.

If Michelle Obama wins the Grammy, she will have one more award than her husband, former President Barack Obama.

scraped.title: Never mind the affair. The real NVIDIA scandal is about illegal GPUs in China. | Blaze Media
scraped.description: The ousting of former NVIDIA CEO, Jensen Huang, sent shockwaves throughout the internet last week. But as everyone debates whether or not his mistress was a Chinese spy or if any company secrets were leaked to the CCP, the bigger story is the advanced NVIDIA chips that illegally ended up on Chinese soil, and how they got there in the first place.
scraped.author: https://www.facebook.com/140738092630206
scraped.h1: Nvidia scandal gets crazier — its top chips were apparently illegally sent to China
scraped.body_text:
Advanced Nvidia GPUs ended up in a Chinese data center, reports say. This is how they may have gotten there.

The ousting of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sent shockwaves throughout the internet last week. But as everyone debates whether his mistress was a Chinese spy or if any company secrets were leaked to the CCP, the bigger story is the advanced Nvidia chips that illegally ended up on Chinese soil and how they got there in the first place.

In October 2022 , the Biden administration banned the leading makers of graphics processing units — namely Nvidia and AMD — from selling their most advanced AI hardware to China and Russia. Under the regulations, Nvidia’s advanced A100 GPU , flagship H100 GPU , and later, the next-generation H200, were set aside for domestic use and sale to select international allies , including the United Kingdom, Canada, Germany, and Japan.

Despite the U.S. government’s attempts to keep the best Nvidia hardware out of Chinese data centers, between 290,000 and 1.6 million advanced Nvidia GPUs reportedly made it to China through last year.

Additional countries — including Iran, North Korea, and Sudan — were added to the ban list in the following years to shore up the United States’ national security and ensure AI dominance.

The Trump administration threw Nvidia and China a bone in 2025, allowing the GPU giant to sell a downgraded version of the H100 to China, which the U.S. government subsequently banned and reinstated amid ongoing security concerns .

Despite the U.S. government’s attempts to keep the best Nvidia hardware out of Chinese data centers, independent research institute Epoch AI believes that between 290,000 and 1.6 million advanced Nvidia GPUs made it to China through last year. No data is available for shipments in 2026.

This estimate is further backed up by claims from AI researcher and former OpenAI employee Will DePue. In a scathing post on X, he wrote :

The question is how.

RELATED: Nvidia CEO admits to affair — as suspected lover is accused of smuggling banned chips to China-linked cutouts

Sean Gallup/Getty Images

Smugglers reportedly used a loophole in the restriction system to purchase GPUs and ship them to an approved international port . The GPUs were then reportedly offloaded to another vessel and brought the rest of the way to China, where they were installed and illegally used to train China’s top AI models.

One of the companies allegedly leading this charge was Megaspeed, a cloud and AI infrastructure group based in Singapore. Originally founded as a Chinese gaming company called 7Road International, Megaspeed was acquired and renamed in 2023 by one Alice Huang, aka Huang Le — the same Alice who later had a romantic affair with Nvidia’s Jensen Huang.

Alice Huang reportedly used her new connection with Jensen to gain Nvidia Cloud Partner status. As an NCP, Megaspeed was designated as an AI cloud provider, permitting it to purchase and install Nvidia's top GPUs in its data centers. So far, Bloomberg found evidence that some of these GPUs were installed in data centers based in Shanghai , and Crypto Briefing reported that more advanced Nvidia GPUs were found unpacked but not installed at a Megaspeed data center in Malaysia .

Alice Huang resigned from Megaspeed in August 2025 , months after she and the company were investigated by Singapore police. During the eight-month investigation, Singapore police held Alice Huang’s passport to ensure she couldn’t leave the country. However, the investigation failed to turn up any incriminating evidence, and her passport was returned, though not before they said she couldn’t return to the country.

Now all eyes are on Nvidia and whether the company was knowingly involved in illegally routing its GPUs to China.

In an interview on Fox News , Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent implored Nvidia to provide answers: “What was the culture at Nvidia?

“And were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings? And I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel.”

Nvidia was quick to comply when the story revolved around Jensen’s affair and Alice’s alleged connection as a Chinese spy. The board wrote in an official statement on November 8:

RELATED: The CEO of Nvidia just resigned over his messy Chinese suspected spy affair. Here's who will probably take over.

Bloomberg/Getty Images

Two days later, Nvidia's board hired former acting United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York Joon Kim and his firm to investigate the matter . Jensen Huang resigned from his post as CEO two days after that.

However, now that the spy narrative is cracking apart , the company has not issued any statements about how the conversation has shifted to scrutinize Nvidia's broader involvement in the plot. Blaze News reached out to Nvidia to clarify if the board and counsel are investigating Nvidia’s seemingly complicit involvement, but we did not hear back by the deadline.

In the meantime, a "Stand with Jensen" petition is gaining traction online with 186,000 signatures and counting. Only time will tell if he is reinstated.

So far, no charges have been filed against former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang or Alice Huang by any government, foreign or domestic. There’s no hard evidence that Jensen knew about Megaspeed’s supposed connection with a plot to route Nvidia GPUs through approved regions to China, nor is there proof that Alice was complicit.

Nvidia has also not been found to have committed any wrongdoing.

Zach Laidlaw

items.summary: On Nov. 16, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced that the NYPD's Strategic Response Group (SRG) will be disbanded.

scraped.title: NYPD’s Strategic Response Group will be disbanded — the mass...
scraped.description: On Nov. 16, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced that the NYPD's Strategic Response Group (SRG) will be disbanded. The SRG is a roughly 500-of
scraped.author: Jasper S
scraped.h1: NYPD’s Strategic Response Group will be disbanded — the mass movement won this, but the fight continues
scraped.body_text:
On Nov. 16, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced that the NYPD’s Strategic Response Group (SRG) will be disbanded. The SRG is a roughly 500-officer unit that has served as the department’s shock troops against protest for over a decade.

For everyone who has been kettled, beaten, pepper-sprayed or dragged onto a bus by the SRG, this is a real victory. But it was not handed down from City Hall. It was won by a mass movement that refused to let a campaign promise die quietly. The work of turning this victory into lasting change for working people is just beginning.

To replace the SRG, the administration is creating a 30 officer “First Amendment Support Team” alongside a larger “Patrol Support Division” that will carry out arrests if the NYPD decides to repress a protest. Under this plan, the SRG may just reconstitute itself as the Patrol Support Division. We oppose the establishment of the SRG under a new name. A key fight in the struggle ahead is to make sure that the SRG and its functions are truly disbanded.

The SRG was created in January 2015 in the wake of the mass uprisings against police terror following the murder of Michael Brown in Ferguson and Eric Garner in New York City in the summer of 2014. The express purpose of the SRG was to repress the movement for Black liberation.

Activists have been fighting for the SRG to be disbanded since it was announced, and now, a little over a decade after it was created, the SRG will be disbanded. This was a hardfought victory won in the streets.

After taking office in January, the mayor repeatedly reaffirmed his pledge to disband the SRG even as the unit kept policing protests. The administration’s first step was a half-measure requiring City Hall’s permission before the SRG could make arrests at protests. In March, NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch publicly downplayed any plan to disband the unit. More than nine months into the administration, the promise remained unfulfilled.

What changed? On October 8th, an ICE agent fired seven rounds at Oscar Belgal, a 28-year-old Dominican man, in Marble Hill, striking him in the neck while his 5-year-old son sat in the back seat. Neighbors and activists immediately mobilized to the scene of the shooting. The movement demanded Justice for Oscar including disbanding of the SRG and the firing of Commissioner Tisch.

The NYPD was not involved in the shooting itself. But the attack crystallized the anger of a city living under occupation by federal immigration agents, and that anger turned toward the entire apparatus of state repression operating in New York.

Five weeks later, the SRG is being disbanded.

This is the lesson every working person should draw: even progressive politicians operate within a capitalist state where police unions, the commissioner, big real estate and the corporate media all exert enormous pressure. The only force that can counter that pressure is the organized power of the masses. A campaign promise became reality only when the movement made the cost of inaction too high.

The Party for Socialism and Liberation understands the police not as a neutral body enforcing the laws, but as a core institution of the capitalist state. The police serve as an organized instrument of repression whose fundamental role is to protect private property and the rule of the capitalist class. Reforms like this are real gains that require us to continue to organize – they must be defended and expanded. But they do not change the fundamental nature of policing under capitalism. With that understanding, the movement should fight to:

Ultimately, the violence of the police cannot be reformed away, because it flows from a system built on exploitation. True public safety will only come when working people hold power and build a society organized around human need rather than profit: a socialist society.

The SRG was defeated by people who refused to stop protesting. Students, immigrants, workers and activists who kept organizing in the face of batons and arrests. Our movement can and must win so much more.

items.title: Skydance takes capitalist control of Hollywood to a unprecedented levels
items.summary: The American movie industry has always been owned and controlled by studio executives who care more about business than any artistic endeavor. But David Ellison conquering Paramount and Warner Brothers means film and television production is now being controlled by a cabal of the most powerful tech oligarchs in the United States.

scraped.title: Skydance takes capitalist control of Hollywood to a unprecedented...
scraped.description: Capitalist corporations are always pushed toward mergers and monopolization. The laws of competition forces every company to drive itself to become bi
scraped.author: Jasper S
scraped.h1: Skydance takes capitalist control of Hollywood to a unprecedented levels
scraped.body_text:
Capitalist corporations are always pushed toward mergers and monopolization. The laws of competition forces every company to drive itself to become bigger and bigger in order to stay above its competitors. When a smaller company goes under, larger companies eat them up quickly. A hundred companies become seventy then thirty and then fifteen until what’s left is a handful of massive conglomerates.

Recently, this process reached a new extreme in Hollywood.

In October 2026, film studio Paramount bought Warner Brothers, another studio dating back to the early days of the film industry. They will now both become divisions of Skydance, forming a new media monopoly in an industry already struggling with over-concentration, cutbacks, and battles over AI and other emerging technologies. Despite the objections of filmmakers and flagrant anti-trust violations, this merger was allowed to proceed with no resistance from the federal government and total capitulation from state officials.

There are stronger reasons for alarm than the usual abuses of monopoly capitalism. This merger puts a massive chunk of American media into the hands of Zionist Tech-Billionaires who are deeply allied to Donald Trump: David Ellison and his father Larry Ellison. It is one step further in a coordinated effort by this small group to take over most of American media and eliminate any voices critical of Trump, Israel, or capitalism.

The owner and CEO of Skydance is David Ellison, son of billionaire Larry Ellison. Larry Ellison is the founder of Oracle, a massive AI and Surveillance company, and one of the wealthiest oligarchs in the world. He is also a personal friend of Donald Trump, contributed $45 million to his re-election campaign in 2024, and has continuously donated to groups supporting the president. In return, when Trump forced ByteDance to sell the operation of TikTok in the United States to private American interests, Larry Ellison was given a controlling stake in the new enterprise. Ellison is also the largest private individual donor to the IDF .

Larry Ellison is also allied with Elon Musk . He sat on the board of Tesa for four years, but more notably contributed 1 billion dollars to Musk’s successful effort to buy Twitter. So this is not the first time Larry Ellison has been the financial support behind the right-wing takeover of a major media company. In fact, he has been funding his son David’s endeavors in Hollywood ever since he founded Skydance in 2006.

The Ellisons’ takeover of American media began in 2024 when efforts began to merge Paramount studios with Skydance Media. In the first year of President Trump’s second term, David Ellison began a campaign of sycophancy to put himself on the new President’s good side. In 2025 he met with Trump twice, promising the President to remove “DEI” practices and turn the network towards glowing coverage of him, the MAGA movement, and Israel. Trump’s FCC quickly moved to approve the merger.

Ellison made good on his promise by appointing Bari Weiss , a fierce, life-long zionist, as the head of CBS News. Ellison and Weiss pretended to be bringing a more balanced and centrist orientation to CBS programming, but it was immediately clear that she was going to move the news station to friendlier and white-washed coverage of both Donald Trump and Israel.

Under Weiss’ leadership, ratings for the news channel cratered. But her job was not to prioritize ratings; it was to neuter the channel and turn it into a pro-Trump and pro-Israel propaganda platfrom. With the tasks assigned to her by David Ellison achieved, she has now gotten an even loftier position in the leadership of Skydance.

After this victory, Ellison quickly began plans to acquire Warner Brothers as well. At the time Netflix had put in an offer to acquire Warner Brothers film studios, but Skydance put in a hostile counter-offer, after which Netflix backed down. Not because Netflix couldn’t attempt to out-bid Paramount, but because the Trump administration told Netflix they would never get federal approval for the merger.

This left David Ellison with no competitors in his bid to obtain Warner Brothers.

Ellison did face some initial resistance from a coalition of 12 states who launched an anti-trust lawsuit against the acquisition. In response, David Ellison threatened to shut down Paramount’s operations in California and move the business to other states, a powerful threat to put numerous California workers out of a job and hurt the Film industry even further.

In the end, what should have been a fierce fight by state’s attorneys generals to stop this blatant monopoly fizzled out into a near complete capitulation. California Attorney General Rob Bonta signed a settlement with Skydance in which all that was attained was a temporary agreement from the production company to produce thirty-plus films over the next few years, keep a certain amount of production in the United States, and appoint a board to monitor corporate interference in the CNN and CBS newsrooms. This toothless and inadequate agreement does nothing to address the larger problems of two of the largest film companies in the world combining into this new behemoth.

On October 6th , Paramount finally finished its acquisition of Warner Brothers, buying the company for $111 billion. In the wake of this victory, David Ellison shared a video ending with a graphic detailing the staggering amount of properties Skydance, his company, now owned. Numerous fiction franchises, streaming platforms, children’s networks, sports channels, and the massive news platforms like CNN and CBS are now all under the domain of one man and his cronies. Before this merger, Paramount and Warner Brothers were two of the “Big Five” studios and titans in their own right. In two years David Ellison was able to buy 40% of Hollywood.

Film and television are among the most effective tools in the hands of the capitalists to shape the thoughts, ideas, and emotions of billions of people around the world. Benito Mussolini famously declared that “cinematography is the strongest weapon” for the newly formed Italian fascist state. Hollywood’s global dominance in the film industry for over a century has been the cornerstone of U.S. cultural imperialism.

Ever since the beginning of the American film industry movies have been used to reinforce racist and capitalist narratives. An early but powerful example is D. W. Griffith’s The Birth of a Nation (1915), a deeply racist pro-confederate film that portrayed the Ku Klux Klan as heroes. After the film was released, membership in the Klan began to skyrocket .

In the century since, the movie industry has been in lock-step with the ruling class’ agenda, never truly challenging its narrative. Movies demonizing socialists as ever-present, devious monsters plagued US cinemas during the Cold War, with films like Red Dawn (1984) presenting the ludicrous scenario of the Soviet Union and Cuba invading the United States.

Continuing into the 21st century, Hollywood reinforced right-wing narratives of Muslims as terrorists and Latin American immigrants as drug dealers or violent gangsters. Once they decided to attack muslims and immigrants at the same time. The film Sicario 2: Day of the Soldado (2018) depicts a moment where Islamic prayer rugs are found in the U.S.-Mexico border. This scene comes from the baseless claims made by anti-immigrant conservatives that Islamic terrorists are constantly walking over the border with ease. It was convincing enough for Trump to make a tweet claiming these rugs were found on the border, with no other evidence than the film itself.

When the majority of depictions of a group are this negative, and these depictions are distributed to millions of undiscerning audiences, it has tangible effects on how those audiences perceive reality. Then it becomes that much easier to launch a war on Iran, occupy a city with armed thugs, or kidnap a Venezuelan president.

The American government is aware of this, and has its own programs for working with the film industry to mystify and deceive audiences.

It’s not a secret that the US War Department has been supporting certain productions in Hollywood for decades. Films like Top Gun (1986) and its 2022 sequel, the Transformers Franchise, and numerous Marvel releases were all made with extensive production support from the Pentagon. Production companies were allowed to film on US military bases, were given military equipment to use in shots, and had US soldiers appear as background extras. In return, officials from the War Department were given approval rights on the film’s script and final edit.

These investments have paid-off; when the original Top Gun was released in 1986, military recruitment saw a surge in success, as high as 500% for the Navy. With its sequel, T op Gun: Maverick (2022), this tactic was repeated and recruiters were posted right outside the theaters playing the film.

The first century of mainstream American film has proven how potently it can serve the purposes of capitalism, imperialism, and white supremacy. But now, with this new merger, how much further can we expect this program to go?

The Ellisons have already shown how they run media companies in favor of genocide and oligarchy. In November 2025 it was reported that Paramount fully intended to blacklist actors who called for a boycott of Israeli film studios. Then in October 2026, an advertisement account for the new documentary Musk on TikTok was suspended right as it was about to reach its wide release.

But their biggest change so far was announced in early November: James Gunn and Peter Safran were being removed as heads of DC Studios. Their replacement is Jeremy Latcham, a Christian nationalist who has said his goal is to produce movies that embrace patriotism, traditional family values, and capitalism. While Gunn and Safran were not political radicals, it’s not hard to guess why David Ellison prefers Latcham to the first two.

The American movie industry has always been owned and controlled by studio executives who care more about business than any artistic endeavor. But David Ellison conquering Paramount and Warner Brothers means film and television production is now being controlled by a cabal of the most powerful tech oligarchs in the United States. What they have planned is a regime of right-wing programming combined with censorship of any criticism of capitalism, imperialism, or Zionism.

Socialist artists were among the first to make films at the turn of the 20th century. The very first school of film, The Moscow Film School, was opened in the Soviet Union in 1919. The following decade in the Soviet Union turned out to be one of the most foundational moments in film history.

That generation of filmmakers was given near absolute freedom to experiment and develop the new artform, and produced works that continue to influence filmmakers to this day. Sergei Eisenstein’s 1925 film Battleship Potemkin remains required viewing in nearly every film school on the planet. They made films that were electric and unforgettable, but also enlightening and educational.

There is a better future for cinema: one where artistic creation isn’t limited to those who have wealthy or famous parents to support them and where everyone involved in the huge collaboration of making film have equal ownership in artistic productions they are creating. Like all other workers, artists should have a say in what gets produced, how many resources get put into it, and receive the full compensation of their labor.

That system is socialism, and when this is achieved, we will see art produced greater than we’ve ever seen before.
